pyqgis_plugin.description: 使用分组树、文件夹树、思维导图、矩形树图或图层属性看板管理工程图层，支持地图主题过滤、同组拖动排序，以及移动、复制、备份物理文件和完整图层样式。/ Manage project layers with group and folder trees, mind maps, treemaps, or a layer property board, with map-theme filtering, same-group drag ordering, physical file operations, and complete layer-style transfer.
pyqgis_plugin.about: 通过分组树、文件夹树、思维导图、矩形树图和属性看板查看与管理 QGIS 图层。支持按当前画布或 QGIS 地图主题过滤图层、同组原生拖放排序、重复数据源大小去重、多选批量修改，以及移动、复制、备份物理文件并保留完整图层配置。/ View and manage QGIS layers through group and folder trees, mind maps, treemaps, and a property board. Filter by live canvas visibility or QGIS map themes, reorder layers within a group, avoid duplicate treemap sizes for shared data sources, batch-edit layer properties, and move, copy, or back up physical files while preserving complete layer configuration.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Raisz-style Relief
pyqgis_plugin.description: Presentation-quality relief rendering from a DEM in the style of Erwin Raisz hand-drawn physiographic maps: two algorithms (hybrid landform and classic oblique hachures) with a shared decoration layer - hypsometric or thematic draped fill, overlay layers for waters, roads, settlements, land cover textures, sheet decoration (frames, graticule ticks, scale bar, compass rose) and old-print emulation.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The plugin builds presentation-quality physiographic relief graphics from a DEM (Alpha & Winter 1971; Raisz 1931; oblique view with proportional displacement - Ridd 1963). Contour levels are made invisible; each relief point is shifted north proportionally to its height, so the higher the mountain, the taller its profile; fall lines with light-dependent density and hidden-surface removal by a floating horizon form the correct oblique view. Two algorithms: "Landform map" (a hybrid of Mower-style morphometry and hachures at working resolution with variable plains density) and "Classic physiographic" (full resolution, uniform hachuring, memory control with optional strip tiling). A shared decoration layer (all optional): monochrome sepia paper, hypsometric fill from elevation (Patterson, Bartholomew, Peucker, Imhof palettes) or thematic fill colored from the QGIS layer style; the fill is draped over the displaced relief; separate water layers (rivers, lakes, seas, marshes) drawn in ink on paper presets and in blue on colored fills; roads; settlements with labels; land cover textures; large-form shading (flat shadow or anaglyptography engraving); sheet decoration (frames including a checkered map border, graticule tick labels in D°MM', old-style scale bar, compass rose) and old-print emulation (dot screen, paper grain, color misregistration). Vector layers are reprojected and clipped to the DEM extent automatically. Output - PNG, SVG or PDF. Requires numpy, scipy, matplotlib, rasterio, shapely (>=2.0), pyproj and affine -- all bundled with QGIS/OSGeo4W.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Network Topology
pyqgis_plugin.description: Toolkit to clean and build the topology of line networks (roads, rivers, pipelines, railways).
pyqgis_plugin.about: Adds a Processing provider with tools to clean and build the topology of a line network — roads, rivers, pipelines, railways: (1) Topology split — node the layer at every crossing (X) and endpoint-touch (T), extending dangles along their direction up to a tolerance; (2) Resolve dangles — directionally extend undershoots and trim overshoots; (3) Collapse pseudo-nodes — merge chains of lines through degree-2 nodes; (4) Connected components — label independent sub-networks; (5) Cluster extents — hull/bbox polygon per cluster; (6) Network nodes — points with degree and type. Output is single-part, geometry and attributes preserved. Built for QGIS 4.0 (Qt6 / PyQt6).

pyqgis_plugin.name: ABCoord
pyqgis_plugin.description: Interactive tool for coordinate conversion, plotting, and inspection across multiple systems.
pyqgis_plugin.about: ABCoord is an interactive QGIS plugin designed for dynamic coordinate transformation. It allows users to input, parse, and plot coordinates from various text formats (such as Decimal Degrees, GMS, and WKT). Additionally, it features a map canvas inspection tool that captures mouse clicks to instantly display coordinates across multiple Coordinate Reference Systems (CRS) simultaneously.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Observearth
pyqgis_plugin.description: Discover, visualize, and analyze satellite imagery with advanced spectral indices directly in QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Observearth is a powerful QGIS plugin developed by the makers of Observearth (https://observearth.com) for discovering, visualizing, and analyzing satellite imagery directly within QGIS. The plugin integrates seamlessly with STAC (SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog) services, allowing users to search, preview, and process Earth observation imagery without leaving their GIS workflow.
Designed for GIS professionals, researchers, agronomists, environmental analysts, and remote sensing specialists, Observearth simplifies satellite data analysis with a fast, intuitive, and efficient interface.
Key Features: • Search satellite imagery using STAC catalogs. • Filter imagery by date range, cloud cover, satellite mission, and area of interest. • Generate and visualize spectral indices such as NDVI, EVI, and many more. • Display imagery directly within QGIS. • Automatic raster rendering with optimized visualization. • View raster statistics including minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation. • Fast loading and efficient processing for large datasets. • Cloud-optimized workflows with seamless Observearth integration.
Whether you're monitoring crop health, assessing vegetation, tracking environmental changes, or analyzing land cover, Observearth provides a streamlined workflow for accessing and analyzing satellite imagery—all from within QGIS.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Parametric Process
pyqgis_plugin.description: Parametric Generative Design and Multi-Objective Evolutionary Optimization Studio for QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Parametric Process is a standalone generative urban design and multi-objective evolutionary optimization lab for QGIS. Build reusable Grasshopper-style visual rule workflows, select urban block/parcel layers, run NSGA-II evolutionary simulations across density, daylight, carbon, and urban quality metrics, analyze Pareto trade-offs, preview 3D phenotypes in real time, and sync reviewed solutions directly into QGIS vector layers. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://geophilo.com/parametric_process/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitLab (https://gitlab.com/geophilo1/parametric_process)!

pyqgis_plugin.name: Raster Statistics Along Line
pyqgis_plugin.description: Computes raster statistics along vector line features.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Extracts raster pixel values intersected by each line feature using Amanatides-Woo traversal and computes per-feature statistics. Supports optional directional raster band.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SateAIs API for QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.description: Run SateAIs SAR satellite detection (ship, oil slick, new building, disappear building, time series) directly from QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: SateAIs is a SAR satellite image analysis platform (currently supporting Sentinel-1). This plugin lets GIS users invoke detection jobs from QGIS, view results as map layers, and manage jobs without leaving the QGIS environment. Requires a SateAIs API key from https://console.spcsft.com.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Flash Features
pyqgis_plugin.description: Flash all, selected, or individual features on the map canvas — from the Layers panel, attribute table toolbar, attribute table right-click menu, or the plugin toolbar.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Adds quick "flash" actions in three places:
Plugin toolbar (two buttons): • Flash selected features — flashes selected features on the active layer (red) • Flash selected vs rest — flashes selected features red and all other visible features blue simultaneously
Layers panel context menu (right-click a vector layer): • Flash selected features • Flash selected vs rest
Attribute table: • Toolbar buttons — same two actions as above, acting on the table's own layer • Row right-click — "Flash this feature" flashes the individual row you right-clicked • Hover — moving the mouse over a row flashes that feature (debounced, 120 ms)
Compatible with QGIS 3 (Qt5/PyQt5) and QGIS 4 (Qt6/PyQt6) via runtime detection. No external dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: quickdraw tools

pyqgis_plugin.name: Kakao QGIS Bridge

pyqgis_plugin.about: Shows Kakao Maps JavaScript API content inside a QGIS dock widget and synchronizes QGIS, Kakao Map, and Roadview in both directions. Includes Local place/address search, Roadview position/direction display, Kakao Mobility route search, route guidance, and route history import/export. pyqgis_plugin.name: ClipToCAD
pyqgis_plugin.description: Copy selected QGIS features to AutoCAD as PLINE/POINT command text. Multi-layer selections, projected metres only, unit presets, and auto parcel-ID labels.
pyqgis_plugin.about: ClipToCAD copies selected vector features from QGIS to the clipboard as AutoCAD command-line text (_PLINE, _POINT, _TEXT) for Ctrl+V into AutoCAD, AutoCAD LT (Real World mode), BricsCAD, or ZWCAD — no DXF export. Local mode (AutoLISP) inserts at a clicked point and scales metres to metric links, Gunter links, feet, yards, or inches. Parcel labels use Auto: each layer's parcel_id or Sy.No if present. FID is never copied as a label. Designed for land surveyors, civil engineers, and subdivision draftsmen.

pyqgis_plugin.description: Batch edit attribute values with prefix, suffix, replace, find and replace, auto increment, fill empty, boolean, and date operations. Please do not hesitate to contact to report errors, problems, or suggestions. Thank you for your feedback and votes.
pyqgis_plugin.about: A powerful plugin for batch editing attribute values in vector layers. Supports multiple operations: Add Prefix/Suffix, Replace Values, Remove Text (with regex), Find and Replace (with regex and exact match), Auto Increment (numbers and letters), Fill Empty (only null/empty values), Boolean (Set True, Set False, Toggle), and Date/Time (Set Date, Add Days, Subtract Days). Works with all features or selected features only. Includes undo support, live preview, and field type validation.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoClick Capture
pyqgis_plugin.description: Verify locations across online, offline and QGIS sources with evidence, review and auditable reports.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GeoClick Capture 2.0.1 provides a unified Location Verification Workspace for comparing online search results, institutional gazetteers, existing QGIS features, polygon or line centroids and manual coordinates. Users explicitly select a preferred source after reviewing transparent trust, agreement and recommendation scores; attach local files or URLs with SHA-256 evidence hashes; create a temporary comparison layer; persist the workspace in the QGIS project; import candidate CSV or shareable workspace packages; and export a ZIP verification bundle containing JSON, HTML, CSV tables, a manifest and copied attachments. Version 2.0.1 corrects workspace persistence on QGIS 4 by using the QgsProject entry API. Earlier capabilities include Review Queue, Offline Gazetteer, Match & Verify, Nominatim search, coordinates, map URLs, snapping, sessions, reverse geocoding and CSV, GeoJSON and GeoPackage export. The plugin supports QGIS 3.28+, QGIS 4 / Qt 6 and has no external Python dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Poprawka odwzorowawcza
pyqgis_plugin.description: PL: Oblicza pole działek z poprawką PL-2000 według polskich przepisów geodezyjnych. | EN: Calculates parcel areas with the statutory PL-2000 correction.

PL Oblicza pole działek z poprawką PL-2000 według § 16 ust. 2 i załącznika nr 3 rozporządzenia z 27 lipca 2021 r. w sprawie ewidencji gruntów i budynków (Dz.U. 2024 poz. 219 ze zm.). pyqgis_plugin.name: RTL Expression Editor
pyqgis_plugin.description: Fixes right-to-left (Hebrew and Arabic) text rendering in the Expression Builder and allows custom autocomplete sources.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
QGIS's built-in editor (QScintilla) does not display right-to-left text correctly, especially when RTL and left-to-right text are mixed. Glyphs overlap and the text cursor jumps to the wrong place, which makes Hebrew or Arabic expressions and layer filters hard to read and almost impossible to edit.
This plugin places an enhanced editor directly above the original one. The enhanced editor renders mixed RTL and LTR text correctly while staying fully sync-hronized with the original editor beneath it, so all existing QGIS functionality keeps working: the field, function and operator tools, validation, value previews and syntax highlighting. Matching brackets are highlighted as well. Nothing in QGIS is modified or replaced.
The plugin also offers an optional advanced auto-complete system. Choose any table or dataset - picked straight from the QGIS Browser, without adding it to your project - and its fields as the source of allowed values, with optional descriptions, groups and group descriptions. Press Ctrl+Space to complete either a field name or a value, and the suggestions adapt automatically to the field being queried and to the layer you are working on.
When a custom auto-complete source is configured, an optional Read Mode switch appears inside the editor. Read Mode shows the value descriptions instead of the stored codes, making a long expression far easier tounderstand, and never alters the expression itself. Where the same code has different meanings in different groups, Read Mode works out the right one automatically from the expression's own surrounding condition, using an optional Group codes column - nothing about this is ever saved to the project. An optional second, alternative description per value adds a third switch position for a different wording of the same descriptions.
The whole configuration, including the auto-complete source, can be exported to a file and imported again elsewhere - useful for sharing a ready-made setup with colleagues.

pyqgis_plugin.name: xDEM
pyqgis_plugin.description: A wide range of high-level operations required for analyzing elevation data.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
This plugin is part of the xDEM Python package, a collaboration between CNES (the French space agency) and GlacioHack (a group of glaciology researchers).
Python dependencies are installed automatically the first time the plugin runs. The installation may take a few minutes, please do not close QGIS during this process.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Topo
pyqgis_plugin.description: L'outil "Topo"/"Topo" tool
pyqgis_plugin.about:
En: Transform the boundaries of geological formations and structural elements into polygons, with attributes derived from the input point layer codes.
Fr: Transforme les contours des formations géologiques et les éléments structuraux en polygones ayant comme attribut les codes issus de la couche ponctuelle d'entrée.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Planes, Trains and Automobiles (plus others)
pyqgis_plugin.description: Animate point to point transport routes without the need for temporal attributes.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The plugin builds animated routes from point layers. Choose a fan-in destination (legs from every place to one hub) or an ordered multi-leg route, and a marker travels along each trail. Vehicles include plane, ship, car, train, or a custom SVG/PNG marker. Every layer is collected into a "route-tracker" layer group and all layers animate together off one shared clock. Playback and the set of animation layers are saved with the QGIS project and restored when it is reopened. Frames can be exported as a PNG sequence (with an ffmpeg command) or a self-contained HTML viewer. This is a visualisation aid, not a navigation product: the coastline mask is coarse and routes may not use canals or narrow straits.

pyqgis_plugin.name: FricMaps
pyqgis_plugin.description: FricMaps: A Tool for Modeling Landscape Connectivity and Fence Permeability.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Resistance surfaces underpin ecological connectivity modelling, yet their construction is often hard to reproduce because it depends on heterogeneous input data and poorly documented preprocessing choices. FricMaps automates the generation of standardised land-cover and resistance surfaces through modular vector preprocessing and a rule-based rasterisation engine driven by a user-editable classification table. It explicitly integrates underrepresented anthropogenic barriers such as fences, applies attribute-dependent buffering of roads and railways, and uses wildlife crossing structures to locally restore permeability at validated locations. Contextual weighting by slope and by distance to any class or custom source supports scenario generation. Outputs are directly compatible with graph-based connectivity software such as Graphab. Source code is GPL-3.0-or-later; documentation and the default classification table are CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE).
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Anthonin Kumm, Cybill Staentzel, Lucie Gendron, Melodie Kunegel-Lion, Sylvain Moulherat, Romain Wenger

pyqgis_plugin.name: Multi Layer Filter Toolbar
pyqgis_plugin.description: Quickly filter multiple vector layers directly from the toolbar.
pyqgis_plugin.about: This extension allows you to select multiple layers and apply a common expression filter to all of them in a single click. It includes a filter history and direct access to the QGIS expression builder.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Another Autosaver
pyqgis_plugin.description: Periodically checks the current project for unsaved changes and always asks whether to save only, save and create a timestamped backup, or do nothing.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Another Autosaver and Backuper checks the current QGIS project at a configurable interval for unsaved changes. Whenever there are some, it asks: save only, save and create an additional timestamped backup copy in a backup subfolder, or do nothing. Nothing is ever written silently. The interval, the number of backups to keep and the backup subfolder name are configurable from the plugin's Settings dialog. Compatible with QGIS 3.x (Qt5) and QGIS 4.x (Qt6).

pyqgis_plugin.name: OVER Catalog
pyqgis_plugin.description: Browse and load the גרסאות לעם (OVER / over.org.il) catalog of Israeli public datasets — spatial layers, tables and live datastore queries — directly into QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
OVER Catalog browses and loads the "גרסאות לעם" (OVER / over.org.il)ת version-tracking catalog of Israeli public datasets directly into QGIS.
an OVER node in the Browser panel (source type -> organization -> dataset), a global search filter that reveals a dataset in the tree, whole-file GeoJSON/CSV loading, a live datastore layer filtered to the current map view, an advanced WHERE/SQL query builder with a field picker, and access to previous versions.
"גרסאות לעם" היא מערכת שעוקבת אחרי שינויים במאגרי מידע ממשלתיים וציבוריים בישראל. המערכת החלה במעקב אחרי המאגרים הפתוחים באתר data.gov.il, וכיום היא מנטרת גם מקורות נוספים: מסד הנתונים של הכנסת, אתר הלשכה המרכזית לסטטיסטיקה (הלמ"ס), שכבות המידע המרחבי של GovMap, פרוטוקולי ועדות, מכרזים, החלטות ממשלה ועוד.
הפלאגין מאפשר לצפות, לטעון ולהוריד את הנתונים שבמאגר. מתאפשרת טעינה של השכבות עם הסימבולוגיה שלהן שאילתות SQL ברמת השכבה וברמת המאגר כולו והתאמות נוספות.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Reuven Kost, Guy Zomer, Shai Sussman

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoBan France
pyqgis_plugin.description: Search French addresses (BAN) and IGN cadastral parcels with GIS tools and A4 print layout.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GeoBan France is a powerful QGIS plugin enabling instant search for French addresses via the National Address Database (BAN) and cadastral parcels via IGN APICarto. Features include buffer creation, spatial selection, A4 landscape print layout with dynamic scalebar, spatial bookmarks, multi-format exports (CSV, KML, memory layer) and interactive reverse geocoding on the map.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Military Cartography Tools
pyqgis_plugin.description: Military cartography, MIL-STD-2525D/E and APP-6D/E tactical graphics, MGRS, and terrain analysis tools for QGIS. Runs fully offline - no external services, no data ever leaves your machine.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Military Cartography Tools (MCT) is a QGIS plugin providing tools for military mapping, including MIL-STD-2525D/E and APP-6D/E tactical graphics (control measures and entity symbols, drawn as real QGIS symbology rather than stamped images, so they scale and print correctly at any map scale, with a per-layer edition switch to choose which standard a symbology layer is built against), MGRS coordinate handling, military grid generation, layout automation, coordinate conversion, cartographic utilities, terrain analysis (illuminated contours, hypsometric tint, line of sight, combined hillshade, and viewshed/dead-ground analysis), and navigation/production tools (bearing/range, GPX/KML waypoint import/export, and batch print-sheet generation tiling a large area). Every tool runs entirely offline against local data - GDAL/QGIS Processing, a bundled World Magnetic Model, and your own DEM - with no external services, API calls, or telemetry of any kind, making it suitable for use with sensitive or classified data.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Urban Growth Predictor
pyqgis_plugin.description: Predicts future urban growth, traffic-density pressure, population density, nighttime activity (economic proxy), heat-risk, green-space-loss, and urban land-use-transition indicators from AOI-only Earth Engine trend data in QGIS 3.x and 4.x.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Urban Growth Predictor uses Google Earth Engine datasets and a spatial allocation model to forecast urban indicators from only an area of interest, a future year, and the desired urban indicator. It creates styled raster outputs and can optionally create polygon vector outputs with class/value attributes and XLSX/CSV trend reports. It reuses the Environmental Assessment Studio Earth Engine dependency and project settings when available.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Q-CensosBo
pyqgis_plugin.description: Query and map the microdata of Bolivia's population censuses (1976-2024) directly in QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about: Access the Bolivian census microdata published by the censosbo project. Pick a census year and table, aggregate any variable by department or municipality (count, mean, median, sum, standard deviation, mode, or the share of a category), review a summary of the result and get a styled choropleth layer. Data is queried remotely with DuckDB, so the large Parquet files are never downloaded. Also covers the finest level of the 2024 census: 268,604 urban blocks and rural communities with the 194 indicators of the INE summary sheet (245 options, counting those that add up both sexes). Includes two Processing algorithms for graphical models and batch runs. Interface and documentation are in Spanish.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SCIMAP Toolkit
pyqgis_plugin.description: SCIMAP tools for catchment delineation, sediment and FIO risk mapping, network index, and flood risk mapping, with a guided panel, land cover risk weighting, and automatic result styling.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Calculates SCIMAP spatial indices including network connectivity, erosion risk, in-channel risk, seasonal FIO delivery risk, and flood mean/stdev outputs using native WhiteboxTools hydrological processing (BreachDepressions, FD8FlowAccumulation, D8Pointer, DInfMassFlux, Watershed, DownslopeDistanceToStream) and a flow-path trace connectivity approach. Tools: SCIMAP Sediment, SCIMAP FIO, Delineate Catchment, Apply Land Cover Risk Weights, Network Index, SCIMAP Flood, Overland Flow Distance to Point, Export SCIMAP Results, and the three SCIMAP Fitted tools, numbered to be run in order (1 Catchment Statistics, 2 Calibrate Weights, 3 Ensemble Risk Maps), which infer land cover risk weights from observed water quality rather than assuming them. A guided SCIMAP panel mirrors the SCIMAP web application workflow with click-on-map pour points and impact points, an editable risk weight table, and parameter set XML that is interchangeable with the web application. Land cover rasters are reclassified into SCIMAP risk weights in the plugin, so no pre-weighted raster is required. Outputs are styled automatically with percentile-stretched colour ramps and can be exported as GeoPackage, KML, point vectors, or Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF. Depends upon the WhiteboxTools executable also being installed. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2010.08.022

pyqgis_plugin.name: PickShift
pyqgis_plugin.description: PickShift: Monte-Carlo estimation of positional and area uncertainty of polygons from GCP planimetric biases.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Polygons digitized from historical planimetric data (old maps, aerial photographs) inherit the positional inaccuracies of their source, yet this uncertainty is rarely quantified. PickShift runs a Monte-Carlo simulation that propagates the planimetric bias measured at Ground Control Points (GCPs) to estimate the positional and area uncertainty of any polygon layer. The bias is interpolated (IDW) over the study extent to produce an error surface, sampled around each polygon vertex through buffered zonal statistics, then randomly resampled over N simulation runs (with optional Douglas-Peucker simplification) to derive, for every polygon, its total uncertainty and 95% confidence interval on area. This plugin is a pure PyQGIS/GDAL/NumPy port of the original PickShift Python script: it only uses libraries bundled with QGIS (qgis.core/qgis.gui, osgeo.gdal/ogr, numpy) and does not require geopandas, fiona, shapely, rasterio, rasterstats or pandas. Source code is GPL-3.0-or-later licensed (see LICENSE). See Jautzy et al. (2024), SoftwareX, 27, 101866 for the underlying method.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Timothee Jautzy, Pierrick Freys, Valentin Chardon, Romain Wenger, Gilles Rixhon, Laurent Schmitt, Pierre-Alexis Herrault

pyqgis_plugin.name: RiverDetectWood
pyqgis_plugin.description: RiverDetectWood: Automatic Detection and Quantification of In-Stream River Wood from Very High-Resolution Aerial Imagery.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Quantifying in-stream wood is central to river geomorphology and habitat studies, yet manual photo-interpretation of aerial imagery is slow and hard to reproduce. RiverDetectWood automates this workflow: it derives NDVI, brightness and Haralick texture indices from a very high-resolution orthophotograph (e.g. IGN BD ORTHO IRC), classifies pixels with a pre-trained Random Forest model, vectorises the wood class and computes per-element size and volume metrics (area, length, width, volume). It is exposed to QGIS as a Processing algorithm ("RiverDetectWood" provider), so it can be run from the Processing toolbox, from the Python console, or chained into Processing models. Requires Orfeo Toolbox (OTB) for the texture computation step, and the joblib/scikit-learn Python packages to load and run the classification model; the plugin can install these automatically from the Plugins menu. Method described in Grimmer et al. 2025 (Environmental Modelling & Software, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2025.106460) and Grimmer et al. 2025 (SoftwareX, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.softx.2025.102042). This QGIS plugin was developed by Romain Wenger (https://romainwenger.fr); the original Python classification tool it packages was developed by Gauthier Grimmer (http://g-grimmer.github.io/). Source code is GPL-3.0-or-later (see LICENSE).
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Gauthier Grimmer, Romain Wenger, Germain Forestier, Valentin Chardon

pyqgis_plugin.name: GISCraft Coordinate Extractor
pyqgis_plugin.description: Extract Geographic (Lat/Lon) and UTM (Northing/Easting) coordinates from point layers, with automatic UTM zone detection per point.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GISCraft Coordinate Extractor is a QGIS Processing tool that extracts point coordinates in two coordinate systems and writes them into new attribute fields: Latitude/Longitude (WGS84, 5 decimal places) and Northing/Easting (UTM, 3 decimal places), along with the automatically detected UTM zone (e.g. "48S"). pyqgis_plugin.name: AQGIS-Sivil3D
pyqgis_plugin.description: Corridor modelling on terrain: extrudes typical cross sections along an alignment, clips them against any DEM, builds the TIN, computes earthwork volumes and produces the drawings.
pyqgis_plugin.about: A Civil 3D reduced to the essentials, inside QGIS. FEATURES: (1) Typical cross section editor built by composing elements -- carriageway, shoulder, verge, kerb or wall, triangular or trapezoidal ditch, daylight slope and benched slope, which can be chained to build a slope that changes gradient at a given height --, with independent left and right branches and separate cut and fill groups, so each side decides on its own whether to excavate or fill; includes live preview over a configurable test hillside, error validation and a JSON section library with nine starting templates, from a road or a ditch to a concrete gravity dam, a rockfill dam with an upstream face slab and an embankment dam with berms. (2) Dynamic parameters: any value can be a number, a V:H slope, a reference to a layer field (@width) or a QGIS expression, resolved once per alignment feature. (3) Corridor computation: a different section per feature chosen by a field, stations at a configurable interval plus the alignment vertices placed on the angle bisector, axis elevation taken from the DEM, from the alignment Z or from a constant value or from an offset above or below the terrain, both of which can also be written into the layer Z (as a fixed elevation or draped onto the DEM) to keep editing it vertex by vertex, bilinear terrain sampling with tile caching, support for any raster GDAL can read and for mesh layers, and automatic warnings when sections cross on tight curves or when a slope fails to daylight. (4) TIN stitched by point code, which lets sections with a different number of benches mesh correctly, with optional merge with the base terrain to deliver a single continuous surface with no gaps or overlaps. (5) Grouped, ready styled outputs: TIN polygons coloured by zone -- cut, fill, at grade and natural ground -- with earthwork thickness; cross sections with red elevation and areas; feature lines and daylight lines; corridor footprint; axis with road symbol; stations labelled as km+m, rotated and offset from the axis; points for every vertex; earthwork table; and a 2DM mesh that QGIS loads as a native mesh layer. (6) Exact earthwork measurement by integration between design and terrain, volumes by average end areas or by the prismoidal formula, and mass haul diagram with a bulking factor. (7) Dockable profile viewer with longitudinal profile, cross section at the current station and mass haul diagram, station navigation synchronised with the map both ways, image export, and a checklist that overlays as many alignments as you want -- from the same corridor or from different alternatives -- in the longitudinal profile and in the mass haul diagram, each with its own colour, while the cross section follows the highlighted one. (8) Automatic drawings generated in paper space: plan sheets paginated with an atlas and rotated so the axis runs horizontally, with a choice of which layers reach the map and whether the whole set of drawings is the main alignment's -- with the others appearing only where they cut its planes -- or every alignment gets its own complete set, longitudinal profile of the main alignment with a data band showing station, ground elevation, design elevation and cut or fill depth, and the other corridors appearing where they actually cut its vertical plane, cross section sheets on a grid fitted to the paper size, and a closing earthwork sheet with totals; with the other corridors drawn wherever they cross or run close, dashed and clipped to the frame, both in the cross sections (their trace on that very cutting plane) and in the longitudinal profile (their grade lines); with standard scales, true 1:1 framing, automatic paper selection, .qpt templates for the title block and export to PDF and DXF. (9) Export and import of the whole corridor as a GeoPackage with its styles plus a JSON holding the resolved sections, which allows reopening it and going on measuring and drawing without the DEM and without recomputing. (10) Several corridors per session as comparable alternatives. (11) Processing algorithm aqgis:corredor for models, batch runs and the console. (13) Longitudinal profile editor: the vertical alignment is drawn with the mouse over the terrain profile using the same digitizing tools as in plan view -- straight, arc, Bezier and NURBS per segment, with control handles and weights -- plus symmetric parabolic vertical curves defined by their length L or by their K value, snapping to the terrain and to round stations and elevations, an editable table of PVIs, multiple vertex selection (Ctrl+click or rubber band) so a whole stretch can be raised or lowered without distorting it, automatic simplification when reading the layer Z so the grade line does not inherit the hundreds of vertices of the plan alignment, live cut and fill shading, feedback on the map in plan view, and writing the result into the layer Z with automatic densification so vertical curves are not lost. (14) Reservoir capacity curve: elevation, stored volume and flooded area of a reservoir or pond from the DEM of its basin, computed by histogram accumulation so the cost does not depend on the number of elevations, with optional clipping by a polygon layer, CSV and PNG output, and the clipped DEM loaded and styled as a water surface with the ramp stretched between its own minimum and maximum. (15) Calculated corridors survive closing QGIS: they are saved next to the project and recovered when it is reopened, or read from the JSON beside an exported GeoPackage. (16) Extensive help shipped inside the plugin. (17) Interface in English or Spanish, chosen inside the plugin itself and not tied to the QGIS locale: menus, dialogs, warnings, generated layer names and the labels printed on the drawings all follow it, and each language keeps its own starting library of typical cross sections. English is the default. Authors: Rafael Vazquez and Claude. Free software under the GNU General Public License v3 or later (GPL v3+).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Easting
pyqgis_plugin.description: Turn recorded deeds, easements, plats, and as-builts into validated parcel geometry. Easting extracts every boundary call with the source text it came from, recomputes the traverse, and checks closure and stated area before drawing anything. Batch folders, DXF and GeoPackage export, filable certificate.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Easting reads a recorded land document (PDF, TIFF, PNG, or JPEG) or a legal description pasted as plain text, and returns geometry you can defend: every boundary call extracted with the sentence it came from, the traverse recomputed, and closure and stated area checked independently before anything reaches your map. Every result carries a GroundTruth verdict, the verification layer behind all Easting products: PASS (closes and corroborates), REVIEW (flagged for human eyes, with reasons), FAIL (not traversable). It refuses to draw geometry a document never described, and says which case it hit. Four document classes ship today: metes-and-bounds deeds, PLSS/aliquot deeds, recorded easements and rights of way, and recorded plats and utility as-builts. Export a GeoPackage, a DXF, or the one-page GroundTruth Certificate of Digitization. Results are kept until you delete them, and History reopens or clears anything this key has run, with every tract drawn back where you placed it. REQUIRES A SERVICE ACCOUNT: extraction runs on the hosted Easting API, so the plugin uploads each document you extract to easting.ai and needs an Easting API key to work. There is no offline mode. You can create an account from the plugin's own Settings dialog in about a minute: three documents are free, no card. The same account works in the browser at app.easting.ai and over the API. See https://easting.ai for keys, pricing, and terms.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Structural Families Mapper
pyqgis_plugin.description: Structural geology workflow: CSV/Excel import with QA/QC validation, GeoPackage layers with geological symbology, Rose/Schmidt/Wulff diagrams with hand-drawn family selection, fault kinematics (P/T axes, tectonic regime) and orientation-tensor fabric analysis.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Structural Families Mapper takes raw structural geology measurements (dip, dip direction, strike, and optionally fault rake) from CSV or Excel, automatically detects and validates columns, and builds a normalized GeoPackage layer with geological symbology. It plots Rose Diagrams and Schmidt/Wulff stereonets -- with great circles, pole density contours and orientation-tensor eigenvector (cluster/girdle) analysis -- and lets the geologist define structural families by hand-drawing a selection directly on the diagram, kept in sync with the QGIS map selection. For fault-slip data it computes P/T kinematic axes and infers the tectonic regime (extensional, contractional, strike-slip, transtensional, transpressional) per family. Includes grouped spatial statistics and PDF/PNG/SVG export. Designed for structural geologists working in mining, exploration and academia.

pyqgis_plugin.name: IGN VueZ

pyqgis_plugin.name: Mapdex for QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.description: Nivo AI assistant for QGIS: ask questions about your layers and PostGIS in plain language, get measured spatial analysis on the map, run Processing, and georeference or digitize scanned maps with Mapdex.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Mapdex for QGIS adds Nivo, an AI GIS assistant that works from your map. Connect Mapdex once, then ask in plain language and let Nivo measure the answer instead of guessing it. You may use Mapdex models, your own provider key, or a local model after connecting. Model inference with your own provider goes directly from QGIS to that provider, while the Mapdex connection owns identity, project context, capability negotiation and the action lifecycle. Every action comes from a closed capability registry: no arbitrary Python, no arbitrary SQL, and consequential steps always ask first. Nivo profiles and styles layers, runs QGIS Processing after confirmation, and sends Mapdex georeference, digitization and validation tasks, adding completed results back as QGIS layers. Provider keys are stored only in the encrypted QGIS Authentication Manager. Needs network access to your Mapdex endpoint (mapdex.ai by default, configurable for self-hosted installs). No external Python packages are required beyond the QGIS standard runtime; works on Windows, Linux and macOS, with Qt5 (QGIS 3.34+) and Qt6 (QGIS 4).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Clip2Place
pyqgis_plugin.description: Clip vector layers to an extent centered on a place anywhere in the world - a rectangle or circle around a point settlement (city, town, village or hamlet), or an administrative boundary.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Clip2Place centers a clip extent on a single place - found worldwide via OpenStreetMap Nominatim search, entered directly as latitude/longitude, or picked from a layer already loaded in the project or from a folder on disk. Three extent shapes are supported: a rectangle sized from a chosen map scale (pick a common one or type your own) and paper dimensions (in mm/cm/in), a circle sized from a plain radius (in m/km/ft/mi), or the place's own administrative boundary - fetched automatically from OpenStreetMap Nominatim for a searched place, or picked as a feature from a boundary layer already in the project or on disk. The tool suggests a suitable projected CRS for the location (its UTM zone, always available worldwide, plus optional additional national/regional candidates when the pyproj library is present) and clips the chosen input layers to the extent. Besides the clipped layers, it also writes the extent itself as a polygon layer and as a line (outline) layer.

Supports QGIS 3/4 and Qt 5/6, vertical exaggeration, track styling, color ranges, time clipping, follow display, native unit settings, camera keyframes, raster image export with configurable format and resolution, plus SVG, PDF and configurable GIF export.

pyqgis_plugin.name: CRS Batch Reprojection – Vector & Raster (Worldwide) [QGIS 4.x]
pyqgis_plugin.description: Worldwide batch CRS reprojection for vector and raster files
pyqgis_plugin.about: A plugin for the batch transformation of vector and raster files - supported by QGIS/GDAL/OGR - between arbitrary coordinate reference systems. The user selects their country from a list of approximately 195 nations (using a search function); a list of coordinate systems specific to that country is automatically generated from the PROJ/EPSG database and displayed in green at the top, while the full list of global coordinate systems remains available below. The country selection is saved (via QSettings). The interface is bilingual: Polish appears above English throughout the plugin. Additionally, in the country/coordinate system selection section, Polish is displayed alongside the language of the selected country (e.g. PL/DE for Germany, PL/FR for France) whenever a translation for that language is available (otherwise English is used). It supports vector formats (SHP, GPKG, GeoJSON, GeoParquet, FlatGeobuf, GML, KML, TAB/MIF, DXF) and raster formats (GeoTIFF/COG, IMG, ASCII Grid, JP2, BIL/BSQ/BIP, NetCDF, GeoPDF, and others supported by GDAL), offering options for resampling, compression, NoData handling, and forcing the GeoTIFF format.

The interface is in Brazilian Portuguese and the data coverage depends on the public FBDS repository for Brazilian municipalities.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Point Shift Tracker
pyqgis_plugin.description: Track how far a point feature has been moved during editing, with live distance analysis and an in-panel warning when a shift exceeds your configured threshold.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Point Shift Tracker adds a dock panel that watches a point layer in the background while you edit with QGIS's own Vertex Tool. Whenever a point's location changes, it compares the old and new position, shows the shift distance on the canvas next to the point, and displays a distance summary directly inside the dock panel (no popups). A configurable Warning Distance highlights shifts that exceed your set limit right in the panel. Page Up / Page Down keys (or on-screen buttons) let you jump between point features without leaving editing mode. Compatible with QGIS 3.x and QGIS 4.x (Qt5 and Qt6).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Field Boundary Tools

pyqgis_plugin.name: 02Agent OSM Downloader
pyqgis_plugin.description: QGIS 3.28+ and QGIS 4 OpenStreetMap acquisition studio with 43 curated presets, Nominatim place search, exact administrative-boundary downloads, tiled wide extents, structured multi-tag queries with exclusion and regex matching, a typo-tolerant offline command router, and safe Processing endpoints.
pyqgis_plugin.about: 02Agent OSM Downloader is a stable QGIS 3.28+ and QGIS 4 acquisition studio for OpenStreetMap. Its 16 thematic groups and 43 curated presets cover scale-aware OSM as-is stacks, urban context, street and rail networks, morphology, buildings, land use, green-blue systems, public transport, religion, tourism, heritage, sport, cycling, cars, traffic, healthcare, education, emergency services and real OSM admin-level places. Urban Context connects street network, built form, trees, public transport and public-realm datasets, and datasets within a theme can be combined in one bounded request. The four-tab dock provides Presets, Query, Command and Agent workflows. Place names are resolved by the OpenStreetMap Nominatim geocoder, which lists every match with its address context and administrative level; when the chosen place has a mapped boundary the download follows that boundary instead of a rectangle, so a district stops at the district edge. An extent wider than one bounded request is split into a grid of tiled requests, downloaded in sequence and merged so an object crossing a tile seam stays one feature, letting a single job cover up to 2,500 square kilometres. A live estimate above the Download button reports the request area and how many requests it needs. A standard OpenStreetMap XYZ basemap can be added from the dock, while downloaded line layers can use OSM highway categories for distinct widths or one uniform width. The structured advanced-query panel combines up to six validated OSM tags with ANY or ALL matching, an optional regex (~) value mode, an optional exclude tag applied after the response arrives, selectable geometry scope, examples, key/value suggestions and a read-only Overpass preview. Every Processing endpoint accepts that same optional exclude tag. Overpass responses persist in an on-disk cache so a repeated download can be instant even after restarting QGIS, and a transient mirror error gets one retry before moving to the next pinned mirror. The offline Command tab tolerates small misspellings, recognises "without X" to exclude a tag, and can check a second dataset from the same theme when a command names more than one (for example "parks and water"). Commands are interpreted entirely on this computer; only a resolved place name is ever sent out. Seventeen persistent map styles provide live palette previews and native categorized QGIS renderers for buildings, roads, rail, transit, water, green space, trees, administrative places and common points of interest. Agent Protocol v1 exposes four stable QGIS Processing endpoints that 02Agent Smart Modeler can discover, inspect and run only after a validated proposal and explicit user approval. API keys remain in 02Agent Smart Modeler's process memory or encrypted QGIS vault and are never copied into this plugin. Downloads use the current map extent, the active-layer extent or a geocoded place, three pinned Overpass mirrors with diagnostic failover, strict area, request, response and feature limits, cancellation, a persistent cache and temporary point, line and polygon outputs. Only four fixed hosts are ever contacted: the three Overpass mirrors and the Nominatim geocoder. The plugin accepts no editable raw Overpass query, arbitrary URL, user path, API key or pip dependency. Illustrated task guides and the full manual: https://geophilo.com/zero2agent_osm_downloader/

pyqgis_plugin.name: PARACUDA-NG
pyqgis_plugin.description: Spectral machine learning: build, validate and apply regression models for spectroscopy and multispectral / hyperspectral imagery, integrated with QGIS raster layers.
pyqgis_plugin.about: PARACUDA-NG (PARAmetric CUbe Data Analysis, Next Generation) is a spectral machine-learning toolkit for spectroscopy and multispectral / hyperspectral remote sensing, embedded in QGIS as a native, dockable panel. A 7-step wizard (Data, Configuration, Preprocess, Model, Validate, Execution, Apply) takes you from loading spectral data through spectral resampling to a selectable sensor grid (Sentinel-2, Landsat 5/7/8/9, EnMAP, EMIT, PRISMA, DESIS, PlanetScope, VENuS and more), preprocessing (smoothing, continuum removal, derivatives, absorbance, baseline correction), and training or comparing regression models (PLS-R, SVM, Ridge, Lasso, MLR, Elastic Net, Huber, Gradient Boosting, Gaussian Process, Random Forest, XGBoost) with optional Optuna hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation. A trained model can be applied directly to a loaded QGIS raster layer, writing the prediction back as a new layer with a matching colour map, or to an unknown tabular dataset. Additional tools include compositional (CLR/ALR/ILR) modelling for parts that sum to 100 percent, a label-permutation and spectral-mixing integrity suite, cross-sensor spectral harmonisation (transfer functions), and a data converter for arbitrary instrument layouts. PARACUDA-NG needs a few Python packages QGIS does not ship (scikit-learn, joblib, optuna, xgboost, rasterio, spectral); it installs them into QGIS's Python on first run, or via Tools then Install Python dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Topoliner
pyqgis_plugin.description: Topology check, cleanup and coverage model for polygon and line layers: snapping, missing nodes, dangles and overshoots, assembly check, topology-preserving simplification
pyqgis_plugin.about: Brings polygon coverages into order. Finds topology violations and separates certain debris from cases that may carry meaning: the first group is fixed silently, the second is only reported and never changed automatically. Snaps neighbouring borders to an exact match without moving any vertex further than the tolerance, inserts missing nodes without changing shape or area at all, checks whether groups of objects assemble into one body, and simplifies while keeping shared borders shared. Replaces the manual routine of snapping a layer to itself followed by a dissolve without attributes. All tools live in the Processing panel and work in models and in batch mode. Interface in English and Russian. Tested on QGIS 3.16 through 4.0. A companion to the Isoliner kriging and contouring toolset (plugins.qgis.org/plugins/grid_isolines) and to Isoliner3D, a standalone 3D viewer for geological surfaces and bodies (plugins.qgis.org/plugins/isoliner3d). Developed with the support of Inform++ LLC (www.informpp.ru).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Interactive Raster Georeferencer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Interactive raster georeferencing directly in the QGIS map canvas using Ground Control Points (GCPs), multiple transformation models, live residual analysis, preview generation and raster export.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Interactive Raster Georeferencer is a QGIS 4.x plugin for georeferencing raster maps directly in the QGIS map canvas. The plugin provides a fully interactive workflow directly on the QGIS canvas: users can select a raster layer, click control points on the original raster and immediately assign their corresponding target map coordinates. GCPs are displayed interactively on the map and can be moved, enabled or disabled, deleted, and managed using Undo/Redo. The georeferencing result can be previewed directly in QGIS before exporting the transformed raster. Requirements and dependencies: The plugin is designed for QGIS 4.x and uses the Python packages and libraries provided by the QGIS installation, including NumPy and GDAL/OSGeo. No separate installation of these libraries should normally be required when using a standard QGIS installation. The plugin does not provide its own bundled copies of external libraries.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Living Legend
pyqgis_plugin.description: Floating legend showing only currently visible layers in map view.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Displays a transparent floating legend showing only layers that are visible in the current map extent. Additional decorations such as north arrow and scale bar can also be activated. The map can be copied into clipboard or even exported as a pdf. The plugin offers shortcuts to the attribute table of the respective element and lets the user edit the legend names directly through the plugin.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Qgis PostGIS Sync
pyqgis_plugin.description: Plugin unique PostGIS pour QGIS : runtime de chargement classé pour tous les utilisateurs et fonctions d'administration déverrouillées automatiquement selon les droits de la connexion authcfg du coffre-fort QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
This plugin enables the creation, population, and synchronization of PostgreSQL/PostGIS databases from a folder hierarchy containing geographic data. It analyzes the directory structure, creates the corresponding schemas and tables, and then imports or updates the layers within the database. 

The plugin also handles the reading, preservation, and restoration of QGIS configurations associated with the data—such as styles, symbology rules, labels, attribute forms, and other settings stored in QML files or QGZ projects. 

When a PostGIS layer is opened in QGIS, the saved configuration is automatically restored, ensuring the layer’s appearance and behavior match the source layer as closely as possible. Compatible with QGIS 3 and QGIS 4.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SDM
pyqgis_plugin.description: A guided wizard for species distribution modeling, from aligning modeling variables to ensemble predictions and generating SDM reports.
pyqgis_plugin.about: SDM is a guided wizard for species distribution modeling in QGIS. It takes presence-only or presence/absence records plus a stack of predictor rasters and walks you through coordinate cleaning and thinning, background point generation, stepwise VIF predictor selection, spatial-block or k-fold cross-validation, and model fitting with nine algorithms (logistic regression, GAM, Random Forest, GBM, XGBoost, SVM, MLP, MaxEnt and ENFA), validating your inputs at every step. It reports AUC, TSS and Boyce across replicate runs, writes continuous and binary suitability rasters, response curves and variable importance, combines the models into a weighted or unweighted ensemble with an uncertainty map, optionally projects onto a second raster stack with MESS and MOP extrapolation flags, and bundles the results into a single HTML report, with every score, response curve and importance value also written out as CSV. Requires QGIS 4.0 or newer.
pyqgis_plugin.tags: biodiversity,species distribution modeling,sdm,ensemble,ecology,habitat suitability,conservation,niche modeling,machine learning

pyqgis_plugin.name: 02Agent Smart Modeler
pyqgis_plugin.description: QGIS 3.44+ and QGIS 4 visual Processing studio with typed graphs, validated AI planning, smart proposals, and native model interchange.
pyqgis_plugin.about: 02Agent Smart Modeler is a QGIS 3.44+ and QGIS 4 visual Processing studio with typed workflows, native .model3 interchange, validated AI planning, reviewed temporary-layer Processing runs, first-class QGIS expressions, and bounded OSM acquisition. Agent Workspace uses compact intent-routed prompts, read-only project tools, and a bounded Workspace (Developer) scope for source inspection, safe diagnostics, and exact reviewed patches; proposals remain inert until an explicit Apply or Run click. Optional Power Mode is off by default and adds full-source SQL, trusted-script, and generated PyQGIS approval cards. Database writes and live in-process Python require a second confirmation; isolated Python uses a cancellable timeout-bounded QGIS subprocess but is not a security sandbox. Connection URIs, credentials, source paths, feature values, and API secrets are not sent as tool metadata. Provider-reported last-request, chat, and cached input usage is visible, with a local preflight estimate and milestone-based large-request notices that never impose an absolute token stop. The 02Agent Urban Context preset can obtain roads, buildings, and trees in one reviewed run when installed; built-in geometry-specific OSM tools remain available. API keys use session memory or the optional encrypted QGIS vault. No pip dependencies are required. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://geophilo.com/zero2smartmodeler/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitLab (https://gitlab.com/geophilo1/zero2smartmodeler)!

pyqgis_plugin.name: Layer Modeler
pyqgis_plugin.description: Enforce stratigraphic order in interpolated hydrostratigraphic raster surfaces
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS plugin for hydrostratigraphic modelling. Adds a menu item to the "Plugin" menu that enforces stratigraphic order across many interpolated raster surfaces at once. Layer boundaries interpolated independently, for example by IDW from interpretation PointZ layers, routinely cross each other where the interpretation is sparse. The plugin clips crossing surfaces to their vertical midpoint in a single pass over the whole stack, replacing the manual pairwise raster calculator workflow. Layers can be marked immutable, such as a terrain surface or a fixed bedrock horizon, in which case crossing surfaces collapse onto the immutable layer instead of meeting it halfway. Adjusted surfaces are written beside their source raster with an "_adjusted" suffix.

pyqgis_plugin.about: InSAR-TS Toolbox provides tools for processing, analyzing, and visualizing InSAR time-series data. Developed at the Geodätisches Institut Hannover (GIH), Leibniz University Hannover. This work was supported by a DAAD (German Academic Exchange Service) Research Grant.
