pyqgis_plugin.name: KUGI
pyqgis_plugin.description:
Plugin untuk standardisari data geospasial sesuai katalog unsur Geografi Indonesia (KUGI).
A plugin for standardizing geospatial data in accordance with the Indonesian Geographic Feature Catalog (KUGI).
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Fitur plugin: - Plugin mengambil skema unsur langsung dari WebAPI KUGI (Badan Informasi Geospasial). - Pengaturan kolom/atribut tabel sesuai standar KUGI. - Ekspor menjadi data spasial baru dalam format Shapefile dan/atau GeoPackage.
Plugin features: - The plugin retrieves feature schemas directly from the KUGI WebAPI (Geospatial Information Agency). - Table column/attribute configurations comply with KUGI standards. - Export to new spatial data in Shapefile and/or GeoPackage formats.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Seto Baruno, Azkal Azkiya, Farda Fadila, Nando Yudanto Aji

pyqgis_plugin.name: AI GIS AGENT
pyqgis_plugin.description: AI GIS automation for QGIS with multi-agent GIS workflows, MCP connectivity, internet geodata and optional machine learning.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
AI GIS AGENT
AI GIS AGENT is an open-source AI-powered assistant for QGIS designed to connect artificial intelligence with real geospatial workflows.
The plugin provides a bridge between QGIS and AI systems, allowing users to interact with GIS projects and supported geospatial operations through natural language and structured AI-assisted workflows.
AI GIS AGENT combines QGIS, Python, PyQGIS, Qt and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to explore new ways of working with geospatial data.
🤖 AI-Powered GIS Workflows
AI GIS AGENT is designed to help users work with QGIS through an AI-assisted interface.
Instead of relying exclusively on manually navigating through tools, menus and processing workflows, users can describe supported GIS tasks using natural language. An AI assistant can then interpret the request and interact with the available GIS tools and operations.
The goal is to provide an intelligent layer on top of existing GIS workflows, helping users explore data, automate repetitive tasks and interact more efficiently with QGIS.
🔌 Model Context Protocol (MCP)
A key component of AI GIS AGENT is its integration with the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
The plugin includes an MCP-based architecture that creates a structured communication bridge between compatible AI systems and QGIS.
This architecture can be represented as:
AI Assistant → MCP Server → QGIS Plugin → GIS Data and Operations
The MCP server provides structured tools that allow compatible AI clients to request supported information and GIS operations.
This approach helps separate the AI system from the GIS application while providing a controlled interface for communication with QGIS.
🗺️ GIS and Project Interaction
AI GIS AGENT is designed to interact with information available in the active QGIS project.
Depending on the available tools and workflow, the AI-assisted system can work with information such as:
Vector layers. Layer names and properties. Attribute fields. Features. Geometry information. Geometry types. Coordinate reference systems. Project structure. Available layers and GIS data.
This allows AI-assisted workflows to understand the current GIS environment before performing supported operations.
⚙️ AI-Assisted GIS Operations
The plugin is designed to support GIS workflows involving operations such as:
Creating and managing vector layers. Inspecting layers and project information. Exploring attribute data. Working with geometries. Working with coordinate reference systems. Creating and analysing spatial data. Performing supported geospatial operations. Exporting vector datasets. Automating repetitive GIS tasks.
The available operations depend on the version of the plugin and the configured AI/MCP environment.
📊 Data Analysis and Automation
One of the main objectives of AI GIS AGENT is to reduce repetitive work in GIS workflows.
Many geospatial tasks involve multiple steps and require switching between tools, layers and processing operations. AI-assisted workflows can help organise and automate supported sequences of operations.
For example, a user may describe a workflow such as:
"Analyse the available layers, create a spatial operation using selected features and export the resulting dataset."
The AI system can interpret the request and use the available tools provided through the QGIS and MCP integration.
AI GIS AGENT does not replace GIS knowledge or professional judgement. Instead, it is designed to provide an additional interface that can assist users during GIS workflows.
🧠 Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
AI GIS AGENT is designed as part of the growing ecosystem of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and geospatial analysis.
Artificial intelligence and machine learning can support many advanced geospatial applications, including:
Spatial pattern detection. Geospatial data classification. Predictive modelling. Environmental analysis. Risk assessment. Feature detection. Spatial data interpretation.
AI GIS AGENT provides an architecture that can be used to connect AI-powered systems with QGIS workflows.
The plugin itself focuses primarily on the integration and communication layer between AI systems and GIS operations. Advanced AI or Machine Learning capabilities may depend on the external AI model, AI client or configuration used by the user.
🐍 Technical Architecture
AI GIS AGENT is developed primarily using Python and the QGIS Python API (PyQGIS).
The project uses QGIS functionality to work with:
QGIS projects. Vector layers. Features. Fields and attributes. Geometries. Coordinate reference systems. Vector data export. GIS processing workflows.
The user interface is integrated into QGIS using Qt/PyQt.
The MCP component provides an additional communication layer for connecting compatible AI systems with supported QGIS operations.
📦 Dependencies
AI GIS AGENT is built around the QGIS ecosystem and its Python environment.
The core technologies used by the project include:
QGIS PyQGIS Python Qt PyQt Model Context Protocol (MCP)
The plugin relies on QGIS for its core geospatial functionality, allowing it to use the existing GIS capabilities provided by the QGIS platform.
Additional Python dependencies may be required depending on the MCP server configuration and the external AI environment used by the user.
🔄 QGIS Compatibility
AI GIS AGENT supports modern versions of QGIS, including:
QGIS 3.x QGIS 4.x
The codebase includes compatibility updates for the transition from:
Qt5 to Qt6. PyQt5 to PyQt6-compatible APIs. QGIS 3 to QGIS 4. 🎯 Who Is It For?
AI GIS AGENT can be useful for:
GIS Analysts. GIS Professionals. Spatial Data Analysts. Researchers. Students. Urban Planners. Environmental Analysts. Developers working with geospatial data. Users interested in Artificial Intelligence and GIS. 🔓 Open Source
AI GIS AGENT is distributed as an open-source project under the:
GNU General Public License v2.0 (GPL v2)
The source code can be studied, modified and redistributed under the terms of the GPL v2 license.
🚀 Project Goals
The main objectives of AI GIS AGENT are to:
Connect modern AI systems with QGIS. Make GIS workflows more accessible. Assist with repetitive geospatial tasks. Improve productivity in supported workflows. Explore the integration of AI and GIS. Provide an open-source foundation for AI-assisted geospatial workflows. 💬 Feedback and Contributions
Feedback, bug reports, feature requests and contributions are welcome.
AI GIS AGENT is an evolving open-source project, and feedback from the GIS and AI communities is important for improving compatibility, expanding supported operations and developing new AI-assisted workflows.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Raster Georeferencer (GCP)
pyqgis_plugin.description: Georeferences a raster image by matching user-picked points on it with entered known coordinates (GCPs).
pyqgis_plugin.about: Loads a raster image, lets you pick any number of control points (GCPs) on it, enter each point's real-world coordinates, and georeferences the image using a GDAL-based transformation (linear, polynomial, or TPS). Compatible with QGIS 3 (Qt5/PyQt5) and QGIS 4 (Qt6/PyQt6).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Raster Importer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Imports raster images and optionally adjusts them immediately to the current map view.
pyqgis_plugin.about: A QGIS plugin to easily import and auto-fit raster images to the current canvas extent via GDAL VRT.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoRemote Tools
pyqgis_plugin.description: Landsat C2 L1/L2, Sentinel-2, CBERS-04A, MODIS 09/11/12/13 scale factor per product independently, PCA, spectral indices, supervised + unsupervised classification, band extraction, vector geoprocessing, zonal statistics and multi-point sampling
pyqgis_plugin.about:
GeoRemote Tools is a QGIS plugin developed by Geomatica Ambiental to automate preprocessing and analysis of multispectral satellite imagery and to support common geoprocessing tasks.
Tools organized into 7 groups:
[Conversion] - Factor Escala LandSat C2 L1 (SR + LST + PAN) - Factor escala Landsat C2 L2 (SR + LST) - Factor de escala Sentinel-2 L1C (10m) - Factor de escala Sentinel-2 L2A (10m) - Factor escala MODIS 09 (Reflectancia Superficial) - Factor escala MODIS 11 (LST C) - Factor escala MODIS 12 (Cobertura del Suelo) - Factor escala MODIS 13 (NDVI / EVI)
[Procesamiento] - ACP Multiespectral (cualquier satelite) - CBERS-04A Pansharpening Brovey 2m - Clasificacion no supervisada (K-Means / GMM / ISODATA / Birch) - Clasificacion supervisada y validacion - Definir celdas nulas - Extraer bandas de imagenes multiespectrales - Firma espectral (Landsat 5/7/8/9 / Sentinel-2 / ASTER) - Poligono superpuesto propio - Secciones transversales
[Descarga GEE] - Descargar imagenes Landsat / Sentinel-2 - Descargar indices espectrales (GEE) - Firma espectral profesional (GEE) - Descargar imagenes Sentinel-1 GRD
[MDE] - Descargar MDE - Generar curvas de nivel intermedias - Generar elevaciones puntuales
[Hidrologia] - Obtener datos climaticos SWAT (GEE) - Obtener variables climaticas Raster (GEE)
[Estudios] - Determinar inundaciones con SAR
COMPATIBILITY: - Qt5 (PyQt5) and Qt6 (PyQt6) via qgis.PyQt compatibility layer - QGIS 3.28 to 4.99
REQUIREMENTS - Python modules bundled with QGIS (no installation needed): - numpy (all tools) - GDAL / osgeo (all tools) - matplotlib (QGIS LTR 3.22+; supervised_classification, pca_satellite)
REQUIREMENTS - External modules NOT bundled with QGIS (must install): - scikit-learn REQUIRED by: Unsupervised Classification (KMeans, MiniBatchKMeans, GaussianMixture, Birch, StandardScaler), Supervised Classification (DecisionTree, RandomForest, NaiveBayes, MLP, KNN, train_test_split, classification_report), Multispectral PCA (PCA, StandardScaler, make_pipeline) - pandas REQUIRED by: Multispectral PCA (variance table), Create Polygons from Table (read CSV/TXT/XLS/XLSX) - openpyxl REQUIRED by: Raster Zonal Statistics (export .xlsx), Extract Point Values (export .xlsx), Classification Report (export .xlsx with charts), Create Polygons from Table (read .xlsx) - xgboost (Optional) REQUIRED by: Supervised Classification (XGBoost) - catboost (Optional) REQUIRED by: Supervised Classification (CatBoost) - earthengine-api REQUIRED by: GEE Descargar Imagenes, GEE Descargar Indices, GEE Firma Espectral, Descargar MDE, Descargar Sentinel-1, Variables Climaticas SWAT/Raster, Inundaciones SAR
Install all external dependencies (run once): python -m pip install --upgrade scikit-learn pandas openpyxl xgboost catboost earthengine-api
Developed and maintained by: Geomatica Ambiental - www.geomatica.pe
Acknowledgments: - Point Sampling Tool by Borys Jurgiel (GPL v2+) - inspiration for the multi-raster point sampling tool. https://github.com/borysiasty/pointsamplingtool

pyqgis_plugin.name: Memorial Descritivo Importer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Detects and imports vertex coordinates from Brazilian land survey PDF documents (memorial descritivo) into a point layer, with automatic format detection.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Reads a memorial descritivo PDF and detects the coordinate format automatically (tries common label pairs, real PDF tables, and a generic pattern that uses the typical magnitude of Brazilian UTM coordinates to tell Northing from Easting), inserting the vertices into an existing point layer. Privacy: the PDF and its coordinates are never uploaded anywhere — everything is read and processed locally. Free for the first 3 uses; continued use requires an active subscription (Kiwify) — only the confirmation e-mail is sent for that check, nothing about the document itself. Includes a manual mode for atypical formats.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Coordinate Picker
pyqgis_plugin.description: Click on the map to capture point coordinates in any CRS, with a running table you can copy straight into Excel.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Coordinate Picker lets you choose a coordinate reference system (or use the project CRS), then click anywhere on the map canvas to capture the point's coordinates. Snapping to vertices and segments of visible vector layers is built in, with an adjustable pixel tolerance, so clicked points can land exactly on existing features — a live snap indicator shows on the map itself when a click will snap. Every click is added to a table with an editable point ID plus Easting/X and Northing/Y (and optionally Latitude/Longitude), which you can select and paste directly into Excel — each column lands in its own cell automatically.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoKlein Raster Optimiser
pyqgis_plugin.description: Converts slow, unoptimised orthomosaics, elevation and multispectral rasters into fast-panning Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs).
pyqgis_plugin.about: Large orthomosaics and elevation rasters from drone photogrammetry or LiDAR are technically correct but practically unusable: no tiling, no pyramids, often no compression, so QGIS or QField crawl trying to pan around them. GeoKlein Raster Optimiser detects what a raster actually is and applies the correct tiling, pyramid and compression settings automatically, with no GDAL flags to memorise: 8-bit RGB imagery gets a real choice between lossless and lossy, and everything else it trusts (Float32 elevation, 16-bit imagery, multispectral) is processed losslessly. It refuses cleanly, with a clear reason, on classified/categorical rasters rather than risk silently corrupting them. A file that is already a valid Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF at the target compression is left as it is; one that is only part-way there, tiled and pyramided but not a COG, is rebuilt.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Shapefile Area & Length Calculator
pyqgis_plugin.description: Select shapefiles from disk or from the current QGIS workspace, and calculate polygon area (m² / ha), line length (m / km), and part counts, in a professional cartographic-themed interface with a resizable results panel.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Pick one or more shapefiles from disk (they don't need to already be loaded into the project) and get per-file and total measurements: area in square metres and hectares for polygon shapefiles, or length in metres and kilometres for line shapefiles. Point shapefiles show a feature count. All measurements use ellipsoidal calculation, so results are correct regardless of whether the shapefile is in a geographic (lat/lon) or projected CRS. Results can be exported to CSV.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Layer file list
pyqgis_plugin.description: Show loaded layers in a non-blocking table and export the list to CSV.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Displays all loaded layers in a docked table with group, name, type, provider, file location, visibility, memory/saved status, and CRS. Includes an option to export the current list to CSV.

pyqgis_plugin.name: KGA Toolbox
pyqgis_plugin.description: Spatial data management, schema, editing, conversion and topology utilities.
pyqgis_plugin.about: KGA Toolbox bundles the KGA processing algorithms into a single provider with a dedicated toolbar. It adds the things QGIS leaves out: a two-way converter between an ArcGIS File Geodatabase and a GeoPackage that carries field domains and layer aliases across, an editor for GeoPackage field domains, an append tool with a real field mapping, a safe attribute round-trip to Excel, a self-contained layer package format, topology checks with an error inspector, and a set of interactive editing tools modelled on the ArcGIS Pro Modify Features pane.

pyqgis_plugin.name: AriesGeo Toolbox
pyqgis_plugin.description: Geospatial productivity suite: Place Finder, AriesGapfill (Landsat 7 SLC-off repair), Mosaic & Cloud Remover, Map Layout Assistant, and Terrain & Hydrology.
pyqgis_plugin.about: AriesGeo Toolbox brings professional geospatial productivity tools to QGIS Desktop across 5 integrated modules: (1) Aries Place Finder: forward & reverse geocoding, multi-provider search (Nominatim, Photon, offline), canvas biasing, batch table geocoding. (2) AriesGapfill: Landsat 7 SLC-off recovery (Single Triangulation, Two-image Global Matching, Two-image Local Moving Window Matching, and Multi-Donor Smart Composite with provenance and confidence rasters). (3) Aries Mosaic & Cloud Remover: preflight raster inspection, VRT & GeoTIFF/COG mosaics, spatial NoData fill, cloud & shadow removal. (4) Aries Map Layout Assistant: 5-step guided layout builder, cartographic templates, coordinate grids, overview insets, and preflight quality auditor. (5) Aries Terrain & Hydrology: elevation diagnostics, slope/aspect/hillshade/contours/TRI, Wang-Liu sink filling, D8 flow routing, Strahler stream extraction, and watershed delineation. Includes 20 Processing Toolbox algorithms.

pyqgis_plugin.name: RoboCOPC
pyqgis_plugin.description: Convert GeoParquet layers to COPC (and back)
pyqgis_plugin.about: Adds "Convert to COPC" / "Convert to GeoParquet" entries to the Layers panel context menu, running pdal translate in the background with a progress dialog, and swapping the converted layer into the tree at the same position.

pyqgis_plugin.name: NLMOD Viewer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Inspect input and output of groundwater models built with NLMOD (NetCDF).
pyqgis_plugin.about: A plugin to read nlmod-specific NetCDF files to inspect groundwater model data (structured and vertex grids).

pyqgis_plugin.name: AriesLegacy
pyqgis_plugin.description: Geo AI automation for smarter spatial-index analysis, multi-index batching, change detection, and reporting in QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: AriesLegacy simplifies satellite-based spatial-index analysis. It supports Sentinel-2 Level-2A, Landsat 8/9 Collection 2, automated band detection, 20+ calibrated scientific indices, two-date change detection, threshold classification, hectare statistics, styled QML maps, HTML audit reports, and a controlled Geo AI assistant. Developed by AriesPlus Geospatial Solutions.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoClassify
pyqgis_plugin.description: Supervised and unsupervised raster land use and land cover classification with advanced spatial validation
pyqgis_plugin.about: GeoClassify provides a comprehensive QGIS workflow for supervised and unsupervised land use and land cover classification. Features include: supervised classification with spectral indices (NDVI, EVI, etc.), multiple ML models (Random Forest, SVM, etc.), unsupervised clustering (K-Means, Iso Cluster), spatial cross-validation, advanced metrics (Kappa, IoU), HTML/JSON reports, confusion matrix analysis, feature importance plots, and spatial autocorrelation detection. Supports NoData handling and post-processing.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Universal Earth Observation
pyqgis_plugin.description: Universal Earth Observation è una piattaforma professionale per QGIS dedicata alla ricerca, consultazione, autenticazione, download e integrazione in ambiente GIS di dati satellitari, ambientali, climatici e geospaziali provenienti da molteplici fonti nazionali e internazionali. Questo plugin è stato realizzato dal Cap. N.M.M. e dal Ten. Col. C.B. del Gruppo di Cartografia Numerica del RGPBIO.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Universal Earth Observation non e' un semplice downloader di immagini satellitari: e' un motore di ricerca unificato che, a partire da un'area di interesse, interroga i cataloghi e i servizi supportati e restituisce un inventario normalizzato dei dati disponibili, con deduplicazione, punteggio di qualita', accesso remoto quando possibile, catalogazione locale e strumenti di analisi. Integra otto fonti: Copernicus Data Space, NASA (CMR, GES DISC, NSIDC, FIRMS), USGS Landsat, Microsoft Planetary Computer e AWS Open Data. La ricerca e' anonima su tutte; le credenziali, quando servono, sono conservate nel gestore cifrato di QGIS. Realizzato dal Cap. Niccolo' Marco Mancini e dal Ten. Col. Cristiano Berretta del Gruppo di Cartografia Numerica del RGPBIO.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Zoom To Predefined Scales
pyqgis_plugin.description: Lock the map canvas zoom to the project's predefined scales.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Adds a toggle button to the Plugins toolbar that, when enabled, restricts every map canvas zoom operation (mouse wheel, zoom in/out tools, rubber-band zoom, keyboard shortcuts, and programmatic zooms) to the scale list configured in Project Properties -> View Settings -> Project predefined scales. When disabled, QGIS zooms normally. The plugin reads the project's own predefined scales dynamically -- it never stores a separate scale list, and it never modifies the project's predefined-scale settings itself. It only affects canvas behaviour while the lock is actively engaged.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoPOI Collector
pyqgis_plugin.description: Collect Point, Line, and Polygon features from OpenStreetMap Overpass and Point POIs from Google Places API into QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GeoPOI Collector creates QGIS Point, Line, and Polygon layers. OpenStreetMap/Overpass supports Point, Line, and Polygon collection without an API key. Google Places remains available for Point features using the user's own API key and is subject to Google Maps Platform terms and policies. The plugin does not scrape the Google Maps website.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Kriging Studio
pyqgis_plugin.description:
Kriging Studio is a comprehensive geostatistical interpolation tool for QGIS 4.x and Qt6. It enables users to perform Ordinary Kriging and Universal Kriging on point datasets, with support for regional linear and quadratic drift components. The plugin includes experimental and fitted variogram analysis with multiple configurable variogram models, anisotropy scaling and direction, and robust prediction workflows.
Key features include: - Ordinary Kriging for spatial interpolation of point observations. - Universal Kriging with linear and quadratic regional drift. - Experimental variogram calculation and fitted variogram visualization. - Multiple variogram models, including spherical, exponential, Gaussian, linear, power, and hole-effect models. - Configurable anisotropy scaling and direction. - K-fold and leave-one-out cross-validation for model assessment. - Prediction variance and standard-error estimation for uncertainty analysis. - Optional polygon masking for restricting interpolation to a defined area. - High-performance local-neighbourhood and chunked prediction for large datasets and grids. - GeoTIFF raster generation with spatial reference, georeferencing, compression, and Float32 output. - Automatic generation of vector contour lines from kriging prediction rasters. - Optional automatic loading of generated raster and vector outputs directly into QGIS. - Automatic management of raster, variance, and contour outputs. - Progress reporting, cancellation support, and robust handling of large interpolation grids. - Automatic refresh of QGIS layers and numeric attribute fields. - Cross-validation diagnostics and configurable graph visualization. - Multilingual Qt translation support. - Native QGIS 4.x and Qt6 support. - Requires NumPy for numerical calculations, matrix operations, vectorized processing, and interpolation grid generation, and SciPy for variogram fitting, numerical optimization, and efficient spatial-distance calculations..
pyqgis_plugin.about: Advanced geostatistical interpolation plugin for QGIS 4.x for spatial analysis of point data using Ordinary and Universal Kriging, with variogram modelling, anisotropy, drift analysis, cross-validation, uncertainty estimation, polygon masking, high-performance GeoTIFF generation, and automatic contour-line extraction.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Ontario Elevation Manager
pyqgis_plugin.description: Download, cache, manage and export native Ontario LiDAR-derived DTM and DSM raster tiles.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS 3.44+ and QGIS 4.x plugin for native Ontario LiDAR-derived elevation rasters. Version 1.2 provides the complete 1 km tile/package workflow for LiDAR DTM and LiDAR DSM, including flexible AOI selection, selective source-package download/extraction, shared or project-specific caching, VRT lifecycle management, cache cleanup, polygon clipping, GeoTIFF/COG delivery, and a responsive compact interface.

pyqgis_plugin.name: geobr
pyqgis_plugin.description: Download official spatial data sets of Brazil as QGIS layers
pyqgis_plugin.about: Easy access to official spatial data sets of Brazil. The plugin offers a wide range of official spatial data sets available at various geographic scales and for various years with harmonized attributes, projection and fixed topology. This includes states, municipalities, census tracts, biomes, indigenous lands, health facilities, schools, favelas and more. All original data sets come from IBGE and other official Brazilian sources and are returned in EPSG:4674 (SIRGAS 2000). This QGIS plugin is built on top of the geobr Python library, which integrates seamlessly with DuckDB and geopandas, and can be used from the Processing Toolbox, chained in Model Builder, run in batch, or called from qgis_process. The geobr library is bundled with the plugin, so there is nothing to pip-install. DuckDB, the engine geobr runs on, is installed for you by the qpip plugin, which QGIS offers to install alongside this one; if you skip qpip, install it into the Python QGIS uses: python -m pip install --user "duckdb>=1.5.3". Everything else geobr needs ships with the official QGIS builds for Windows and macOS; a Linux distribution build of QGIS may lack geopandas or pyarrow, and the plugin says so at startup.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS LAB
pyqgis_plugin.description: Read, search and bookmark QGIS LAB articles inside QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Read QGIS LAB articles and images in a native reader, search all articles and keep bookmarks across sessions. Uses only QGIS and its bundled Qt; no extra packages or browser engine required.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Palm Gap Detector
pyqgis_plugin.description: Detect probable missing oil palm positions from georeferenced palm points by analyzing real planting rows and spacing gaps.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Palm Gap Detector analyzes georeferenced oil palm points in projected coordinate systems and detects probable missing palms by finding large spacing jumps within real planting rows. The tool is designed for oil palm plantations and assumes a triangular/staggered planting system. It supports optional lot polygons, multiple optional exclusion layers for roads, streams, drains, buildings or non-plantable areas, confidence labels, sequence and cluster indicators, and export to temporary memory layer, GeoPackage or Shapefile. Detected gap points that fall inside an exclusion layer or its buffer are omitted from the output. This version includes QGIS 3.x and QGIS 4.x / Qt5 and Qt6 compatibility updates and resolves QGIS plugin repository Bandit security scan warnings related to silent exception handling and Qt6 compatibility warnings. For best results, use vector layers in a projected CRS with meter units.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Find Value
pyqgis_plugin.description: Find and zoom to selected feature by value
pyqgis_plugin.about: Find Value plugin allows users to search records by field value, select matching features and automatically zoom to results.

pyqgis_plugin.name: ATLAS Geo-Dock
pyqgis_plugin.description: QGIS integrated plugin for UAV Pose Estimation and UAV-to-Map Registration with batch processing and advanced alignment options
pyqgis_plugin.about: ATLAS Geo-Dock registers UAV imagery to reference maps using AI-powered pose estimation. Features include a 5-step rotation sweep, batch image processing, auto-scaling and interactive preview mapping. HOSTED SERVICE: georeferencing does not run on your machine. The images you select and the results produced are uploaded to and processed by AIVE AI Systems' hosted ATLAS service, so an ATLAS account and a working internet connection are required to use the plugin. AVAILABILITY: this plugin is downloadable worldwide, but access to the ATLAS service is limited to approved jurisdictions, and an account may not be usable outside them. DEPENDENCIES: none beyond a standard QGIS installation. The plugin uses the GDAL and Qt libraries QGIS already ships.

pyqgis_plugin.name: AI Agent by TerraLab
pyqgis_plugin.description: Your AI agent for QGIS. Hand it the work and it finds the data, runs the analysis, styles the map and builds the layout. 285+ tools and 60 open data connectors.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
It works on your own layers, in the project you already have open, and shows each step as it goes.
• 285+ tools: load and inspect data, style and label maps, run Processing algorithms, edit geometry, build print layouts
• 60 open data connectors: OpenStreetMap, Copernicus, NASA, USGS, IGN, Overture, Planetary Computer and 53 more
• A catalog of 530+ ready datasets, from national sources in 97 countries and from EU-wide and global ones, each with its licence
• You stay in control: you see every step before it runs, changes wait for your approval, and one click undoes anything it changed
• Fits your habits: one conversation per project, and attach files, layers, selections or the map view to a message
• Works with AI Edit and AI Segmentation when those TerraLab plugins are installed
• 12 languages: English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Indonesian, Japanese, Chinese (simplified and traditional)
• Answers come from an AI model. It can be wrong; review what it changes
• Sends your request and a description of the open project to agent.terra-lab.ai, in the European Union. Your layers and files stay on your machine. See https://terra-lab.ai/privacy-policy

pyqgis_plugin.about: Standalone toolbar tool that creates separate GeoTIFF clips from a single raster using polygon or grid features and a selected attribute field for automatic filenames.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QuickBDOT
pyqgis_plugin.description: Download, select, export and visualize Polish BDOT10k topographic data directly in QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QuickBDOT is a QGIS plugin for downloading, selecting, exporting and visualizing Polish BDOT10k topographic data. It supports the current map extent, polygon layer geometry and interactive county selection. Data can be exported to GeoPackage or Shapefile with optional BDOT10k symbology and labels. The plugin is intended for data covering Poland and does not require external Python packages.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Layer CRS Display
pyqgis_plugin.description: Displays layer CRS, audits a project's CRS consistency, and batch reprojects selected vector and raster layers.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Displays layer CRS without renaming original layers. The read-only project audit identifies matching, different and missing CRS definitions and can send selected mismatches to the existing batch reprojection workflow. Batch reprojection saves selected vectors to GeoPackage and GDAL rasters to GeoTIFF. Requires Processing and its GDAL provider for rasters. Supports QGIS 3 and QGIS 4.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Qgis Advanced Map Tips&Actions
pyqgis_plugin.description: Advanced Map Tips and Actions Studio for vector and raster layers with Qt-safe HTML cards, inline charts, and 1-click web/spatial actions.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Interactive HTML MapTips, micro-charts (progress bars, SVG donuts, sparklines), one-click dynamic spatial actions, and live raster HUD inspection for QGIS. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://geophilo.com/qgis_maptips/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitLab (https://gitlab.com/geophilo1/qgis_maptips)! Qgis Advanced Map Tips&Actions is an advanced Map Tips and Actions Studio designed for both vector and raster layers in QGIS 3.28+ and QGIS 4. It bridges the gap between raw attribute tables and modern interactive map exploration by providing a palette-aware, dockable card designer, zero-dependency micro-charts, and a 1-click action library.
Key Capabilities: - Palette-Aware Dockable Studio: Automatically adapts to light, dark, and high-contrast QGIS themes. - Universal Layout Archetypes: Modern KPI cards, comparison progress bars, multi-metric inline SVG donut charts, photo/media cards, and raster HUD cards. - Zero-Dependency Inline Charts: Generates bulletproof HTML tables and pure SVG data-URIs that render natively inside Qt QTextDocument without external JavaScript or browser overhead. - 1-Click Action Hub: Dynamic CRS-aware web actions (Google Maps, Street View, Yandex Maps, TKGM Cadastre), local document/photo viewers, and clipboard exports. - Live Canvas HUD: Optional non-intrusive hover inspector for raster pixel sampling and multi-layer point inspection with configurable dwell-time debouncing. - Native Persistence: Injected map tips and actions write directly to the layer style and QgsActionManager, remaining fully functional when shared with users who do not have the plugin installed.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS Project Snapshot
pyqgis_plugin.description: Take your QGIS project offline: download WMS/WMTS maps and XYZ tiles (e.g. OpenStreetMap), and keep vector data, styles and a report.
pyqgis_plugin.about: EN: Take your QGIS project offline with vectors, lossless maps, styles and a report. Download WMS/WMTS maps and XYZ tiles, such as OpenStreetMap basemaps, for offline use. It downloads in parallel, adapts to your computer and servers, and resumes interrupted work. With many layers and a large area, especially at zoom levels above 17, the tile count can be huge and downloads may take several hours to several days. You'll need QGIS 3.40+/4.x, Python >=3.10 and GDAL >=3.7 supplied by QGIS, access to your sources and disk space. Includes defusedxml (PSF license); no extra Python packages to install. Install the release ZIP through the QGIS Plugin Manager, then restart QGIS. It runs locally, without analytics or sending projects/diagnostics to the author. Requests send the required area, layer settings and authentication to your chosen services. Please respect their licenses, attribution and download/reuse limits; the author isn't liable for users' violations to the extent permitted by law. GPL-2.0-only. Built with help from AI/vibe coding and tested (Bandit, secret scanning, Qt6 checks, Ruff/Flake8, proxy/error handling, integrity and crash recovery). PL: Zabierz projekt QGIS do pracy offline, razem z wektorami, bezstratnymi mapami, stylami i raportem. Pobierz mapy WMS/WMTS i kafelki XYZ, np. podkłady OpenStreetMap, do pracy bez sieci. Wtyczka pobiera równolegle, dobiera obciążenie do komputera i serwerów oraz pozwala wznowić przerwaną pracę. Przy wielu warstwach i dużym obszarze, zwłaszcza przy zoomie powyżej 17, liczba kafelków może być ogromna, a pobieranie potrwać od kilku godzin do kilku dni. Potrzebujesz QGIS 3.40+/4.x, Pythona >=3.10 i GDAL >=3.7 z QGIS, dostępu do źródeł i miejsca na dysku. Zawiera defusedxml (licencja PSF); bez instalowania dodatkowych pakietów Pythona. Zainstaluj ZIP przez Menedżer wtyczek i uruchom QGIS ponownie. Wszystko odbywa się na Twoim komputerze, bez analityki i wysyłania projektu/diagnostyki do autora. Zapytania przekazują usługom potrzebny zasięg, ustawienia warstw i uwierzytelnienie. Pamiętaj o licencjach, podawaniu źródeł i ograniczeniach pobierania/użycia danych; w granicach prawa autor nie odpowiada za naruszenia użytkownika. GPL-2.0-only. Powstała z pomocą AI i vibe codingu; przeszła testy (Bandit, skan sekretów, Qt6, Ruff/Flake8, proxy/błędy, integralność i wznowienie po awarii).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Quick Inspector
pyqgis_plugin.description: Universal geometry inspector for quickly analyzing points, lines, and polygons, including coordinates, lengths, areas, and other key geometric properties. Copy or export results as WKT, GeoJSON, or coordinates.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Quick Inspector lets you click a feature directly on the map and instantly view the most relevant geometric information based on its geometry type. For points, it displays latitude/longitude, X/Y coordinates, and CRS information. For lines, it provides length, vertex count, and start/end coordinates. For polygons, it shows area, perimeter, vertex count, and centroid. The plugin also displays the feature's attribute table and allows individual attribute values to be edited through a dedicated dialog with Save and Cancel options. Geometric information can be copied to the clipboard or exported to WKT, GeoJSON, or coordinate-list files.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SecureGeoPackage
pyqgis_plugin.description: Encrypt tables and columns inside a GeoPackage, grant access by public key with roles, and open what you are allowed to read. The file stays a valid GeoPackage.
pyqgis_plugin.about: SecureGeoPackage implements the egpkg_encryption GeoPackage extension. Seal whole layers or single columns of any GeoPackage; the unsealed layers stay readable for everyone in any GIS. Access is granted to public identities (keys, never passwords) with roles: reader, contributor, writer, admin. A signed public header shows who may do what under pseudonyms; names live encrypted. Rows of encrypted-column tables carry the author's and the validator's signature, so a contributor's rows stay pending until a writer validates them. Identities live in the QGIS Authentication Manager or the platform key store and move between machines with a one-time code. Dependencies: none beyond QGIS; all cryptography is pure Python and bundled. Optional: the "cryptography" package as an accelerator when present; on macOS the system "security" tool and on Linux "secret-tool" (libsecret) for the OS key store, otherwise the QGIS Authentication Manager is used. A private production by Captain Ahab & Cosmo, GPL-3.0-or-later (full attribution in the bundled LICENSE).

pyqgis_plugin.name: EarthWorkQ
pyqgis_plugin.description: Earthwork cut and fill quantities by weighted grid integration, with void-ratio volume conversion, cross-validated interpolation and a verifiable calculation report
pyqgis_plugin.about: EarthWorkQ integrates cut and fill volumes between a surveyed existing ground surface and a design formation over one or more polygons, and solves for the formation level at which a site balances. METHOD. All elevation inputs are reduced to a common aligned grid. Boundary cells are area-weighted by rasterising the area of interest at a sub-cell resolution (8x8 by default) and block-averaging, rather than being included or excluded whole on a centre-in-polygon test, which otherwise introduces an error proportional to the site perimeter. Volumes are the coverage-weighted sum of the signed depth field over cell area. No engine extrapolates: cells outside the convex hull of the survey, or beyond the outermost contour, are returned as nodata, excluded from the quantities, and reported as an area shortfall. VOLUME CONVERSION. Cut and fill are related by conservation of the volume of solids, V_solids = V_total / (1 + e), giving a shrinkage factor of (1 + e_in-situ) / (1 + e_compacted). Material may be specified by void ratios, by dry densities, or by an in-situ density with a compaction requirement as a percentage of Proctor maximum dry density. Water content is excluded from the volume balance, since it is not conserved through conditioning and compaction; it is used only for conditioning water volume, haulage mass, and validation that the implied degree of saturation S = w.Gs/e does not exceed unity. An optional loose void ratio gives bulked haul volume; an optional topsoil strip depth is reported separately and offsets the earthworks surface. INTERPOLATION. Engines are swappable and filtered by input type: Clough-Tocher and linear Delaunay TIN, thin-plate RBF with tension and smoothing, inverse distance weighting, nearest neighbour, GRASS v.surf.rst, GRASS r.surf.contour, and the native QGIS TIN. Ten-fold cross-validation runs over every applicable engine and reports RMSE, MAE, bias and maximum error, so the interpolator is selected by measurement rather than by assumption. Contour input defaults to r.surf.contour, which distance-weights between bracketing contours rather than triangulating vertices and so avoids the flat-triangle artefacts that produce level hilltops and valley floors. Contour topology is validated for crossing lines at differing elevations, and polylines are densified before fitting. BALANCE ANALYSIS. Sorted cumulative sums of the coverage-weighted ground elevations reduce cut and fill at any level to a binary search, making a full sweep effectively free; the balance level satisfying cut = SF x fill is then found by bisection on a monotone function. The level of minimum total earthmoving is reported alongside it. VERIFICATION. A grid convergence test recomputes quantities at half and a quarter of the chosen cell size. Where the design surface is planar, an independent exact TIN prismatic integration is performed, with triangles straddling the zero plane split at the intersection and integrated in closed form. Interpolation RMSE is propagated to an indicative volume uncertainty. INPUTS. CSV or XLSX table of easting, northing and elevation; point layer with elevation from an attribute or geometry Z; contour polylines; or an existing DEM. Design surfaces may be a flat formation level, a sloped plane defined by a spot level and grades in X and Y, or a design DEM. All inputs must be in a projected CRS in metres or feet. OUTPUTS. Signed cut/fill depth raster with a diverging ramp centred on zero, existing and design surface rasters, cut/balanced/fill zone polygons, depth contours, per-polygon quantities as CSV and as layer attributes, balance curve and area-elevation charts, and an HTML calculation report recording every input, assumption and check. The engine is also exposed as three Processing algorithms for model builder, batch and PyQGIS use.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoCad UAV Toolkit
pyqgis_plugin.description: Technical suite for forestry design and UAV photogrammetry: parametric CAD with automatic Italian cadastral lookup, reforestation planning on a DEM, and flight mission planning with real terrain following.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
GeoCad UAV Toolkit is a QGIS plugin for integrated geospatial work: technical CAD drawing, reforestation design, and UAV photogrammetric mission planning. The three modules share one geometry engine, one terrain model and one cadastral service.
CAD. Parametric geometry -- square, rectangle, regular polygon, circle, arc, line, polyline -- with dimensional input (side, angle, radius) and native QGIS snapping. Move, rotate and resize preserve the construction parameters. Every shape placed queries the cadastre on its own geometry rather than on a point: the attribute table carries five columns (Area, Perimeter, Municipality, Sheet, Parcel) and the full reading -- every municipality, every sheet, every parcel, with cadastral area, intersected area and percentage -- stays in the panel and on the map.
REFORESTATION. A sixteen-step workflow: area definition, cadastral data, elevation model, constraints and setbacks, homogeneous zones, species catalogue and composition, density and planting pattern with trigonometric slope correction, row orientation, plant generation, naturalistic pass (glades, irregularity, per-species minimum distances), comparative optimisation, anomaly checks, plant editing on the layer, map composition and deliverables.
UAV. Photogrammetric planning in twelve steps: mission area from a polygon or from a linear axis for corridors, drone and sensor libraries, bidirectional GSD calculator (flight height and ground resolution are two ends of the same optical relation), real terrain following on the DEM with an elevation profile, acquisition parameters and overlaps, strip generation with a measured azimuth, waypoints and exposure stations, safety checks against obstacles and endurance, mission preview on the map, flight simulation with ground footprints and live coverage, pre-flight validation and export.
CADASTRE. Queries the INSPIRE WFS service of the Italian Agenzia delle Entrate, with real geometric intersection. A geometry spanning several municipalities returns all of them, every sheet and every parcel involved, each with its cadastral area, intersected area, percentage of the parcel and percentage of the project; Belfiore codes are resolved to municipality names. Large bounding boxes are tiled, merged and deduplicated, so a provider that stops at its own feature ceiling does not silently truncate the answer. The same engine serves the CAD module and the reforestation module.
DEM AND TERRAIN. One terrain model for the whole plugin: slope and aspect for the planting pattern, flight height for the UAV mission. The raster is reprojected from the CRS the QGIS layer declares, which is the one QGIS draws it with. Waypoint heights really follow the ground.
CARTOGRAPHY AND EXPORT. Map sheets on QgsPrintLayout from A4 to A0, portrait and landscape, with legend, scale bar, north arrow and grid. Reports in PDF, Word and Excel. Missions in GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, CSV, Litchi, MAVLink and native DJI WPML, the last one restricted to the aircraft DJI documents as compatible.
INTEGRATION. GIS, CAD, cadastre, reforestation, UAV, photogrammetry and cartography work on the same data: the area drawn with the CAD tools is the reforestation project area, the reforestation DEM is the terrain following DEM, and the forestry project generates the flight mission that documents it.
Interface and reports are in Italian.
Created by Cap. Niccolò Marco Mancini — RGPBIO.

pyqgis_plugin.name: EchoCad
pyqgis_plugin.description: Import DXF drawings into QGIS with CAD layers, colours, line types, hatch patterns and text intact. DWG is opened directly by EchoCad Pro.
pyqgis_plugin.about: EchoCad reads DXF drawings the way they were drawn: one QGIS layer per CAD layer, entity colour, line type and line width carried over, hatch patterns rebuilt from the drawing's own definitions, and text at its original size, rotation and colour. Everything runs locally - drawings never leave your machine. QGIS itself cannot open DWG files newer than the 2000 format. This free edition reads DXF (save as DXF from the CAD you use). EchoCad Pro opens DWG (R14 to 2018 and newer) directly in QGIS with a bundled converter, works offline on closed networks, and adds block attribute extraction, batch folder conversion and layer mapping profiles: https://echocad.pages.dev. The interface follows your QGIS language: English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese and Chinese are included.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SVG to QGIS Style
pyqgis_plugin.description: Converts SVG symbols (single file or entire folder) into a single QGIS style file (.xml), with preview and customization of background and fill colors.
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin allows you to select one or more SVG files (including from an entire folder and its subfolders) and generate a single QGIS style file (.xml) that can be imported into the Style Manager. You can view a 64x64 preview of each icon, apply custom background and fill colors to all or only selected items, and restore the original colors at any time.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Acervo SIG - CPRM
pyqgis_plugin.description:
Catalogo do acervo GEOSGB do Servico Geologico do Brasil (SGB/CPRM) diretamente no QGIS: pesquise, baixe e adicione dados ao projeto.
Catalog of the GEOSGB collection of the Geological Survey of Brazil (SGB/CPRM) inside QGIS: search, download and add data to your project.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Acesso a 4.719 camadas e 643 GB de dados, com busca por folha, projeto ou palavra-chave, downloads em segundo plano e selecao por pacote. Suporta diversos formatos, incluindo SHP, KML, KMZ, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, LAS/LAZ, XLSX, CSV e a carta geologica em PDF. Tambem permite converter XYZ do Geosoft em pontos e espacializar planilhas de geoquimica. O catalogo e embutido e atualizavel pelo repositorio, sem dependencias externas.
Access to 4,719 layers and 643 GB of data, with search by map sheet, project or keyword, background downloads and per-package selection. Supports many formats, including SHP, KML, KMZ, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, LAS/LAZ, XLSX, CSV and the geological map as PDF. It also converts Geosoft XYZ files into point layers and turns geochemistry spreadsheets into layers. The catalog is bundled and updatable from the repository, with no external dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: HydroGeomorphology Tools for QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.description: A plugin to support hydrological, geomorphological and watershed management planning in mountain basins, developed by HydroLab uniUD (https://hydrolab.uniud.it/)
pyqgis_plugin.about: The HydroGeomorphology Tools for QGIS is a plugin that provides (i) Algorithms for hydro-geomorphology analyses and hydrological modelling; (ii) Workflows for sediment connectivity assessment; (iii) Functions useful for the analysis and processing of multi-temporal Digital Terrain Models; (iv) A set of tools to support mapping and updating of torrent control structures databases.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Scout - AI Geospatial Catalog
pyqgis_plugin.description: Publish QGIS layers to Scout and load them back as PMTiles, GeoParquet, GeoPackage, WFS or XYZ tiles. Ask AI questions about your data and get results as map layers.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Scout QGIS Plugin lets you publish any vector layer from QGIS to Scout, making it instantly available as PMTiles, GeoParquet, GeoPackage, WFS, XYZ vector tiles, and an HTML web map. Browse your Scout catalog and add any format directly to the QGIS layer panel for analysis or use as basemap tiles. AI-powered suggestions analyse each dataset's schema to recommend the best questions to ask — answers are returned as GeoPackage or GeoParquet layers loaded directly on your map. Available on Free, Solo, Professional, and Enterprise (Custom) plans.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Scratch-X
pyqgis_plugin.description: Fast, lightweight scratch geometry creation tool for QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about: Scratch-X is a free QGIS plugin for quickly creating Line, LineString routes, Point, Polygon, and customizable Shapes directly on the QGIS map canvas, with live measurements, automatic edge-pan while drawing, categorized symbols, automatic file saving, and export to SHP, TAB, KML, or GeoJSON.

pyqgis_plugin.name: OpenTopography Point Elevation
pyqgis_plugin.description: Create a point layer with OpenTopography elevation values using a QGIS Processing algorithm.
pyqgis_plugin.about: OpenTopography Point Elevation uses the OpenTopography Point Elevation API to create a new copy of an input point layer containing elevation, dataset, vertical CRS EPSG and unit fields. The toolbar icon, Vector menu and Processing Toolbox all open the same Processing algorithm. Inspired by and credited to the OpenTopography DEM Downloader QGIS plugin by Kyaw Naing Win.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Continental Boundary Loader Search
pyqgis_plugin.description: Search and load offline continental administrative boundaries from the QGIS Coordinate field.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Adds offline autocomplete for 525 global, continental and administrative boundaries to QGIS's existing Coordinate field while preserving normal coordinate entry.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Tanzania Boundary Search
pyqgis_plugin.description: Search and load Tanzania administrative boundaries from the QGIS Coordinate field.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Adds offline autocomplete for 3,881 Tanzania country, region, district and ward boundaries to QGIS's existing Coordinate field while preserving normal coordinate entry.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Copy Vector as GeoJSON
pyqgis_plugin.description: Copy vector layers, selected features and bounding boxes to the clipboard as GeoJSON.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Adds Copy as GeoJSON and Copy BBOX commands to the vector-layer context menu and includes a configurable Processing Toolbox algorithm. Geometry can be transformed to EPSG:4326 or another selected CRS before copying.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GIS Work Agent
pyqgis_plugin.description: Prompt-driven GIS work assistant for QGIS that turns simple everyday text into vector, raster, table and multi-step Processing workflows.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GIS Work Agent lets users describe GIS tasks in ordinary language and converts them into safe QGIS Processing workflows. It includes beginner-friendly prompt interpretation, context-aware prompt suggestions, active-layer fallback, multi-step workflow planning, vector and raster operations, Processing Toolbox discovery, preview-before-run, prompt history, output management and detailed diagnostics. The toolbar icon changes state while the agent is running and after success or failure. Prompt text is translated into QGIS parameters and is never executed as Python or shell code. Compatible with QGIS 3.28+ and QGIS 4.x through qgis.PyQt.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Mr. Akmaul Hoque; Dr. Manish Kumar Naskar; Dr. Debasish Chakraborty

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS Profile Migrator
pyqgis_plugin.description: Export, inspect and safely import selected QGIS profile settings and resources.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Moves selected parts of a configured QGIS profile to another QGIS installation using a portable archive with a JSON manifest, checksums and CSV inventory. Import supports a dry-run preview and automatic backup.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QR Code Generator
pyqgis_plugin.description: Generate customizable QR codes and linear barcodes for QGIS and Print Layout.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Creates QR codes and common linear barcodes from links, text or product values, with selectable foreground and background colours, live preview, PNG export, clipboard copy and direct insertion into QGIS Print Layout as editable Picture items.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoFlow Guide
pyqgis_plugin.description: Layer-aware QGIS guidance for exploring data, managing selections, CRS-aware buffers, geometry processing and raster display.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
GeoFlow Guide is a layer-aware, beginner-friendly QGIS plugin that recommends suitable GIS tasks in plain English based on the active layer type. It supports Point, Line, Polygon and Raster layers and performs all operations directly inside QGIS.
### Available Features
- Automatically detects the active layer type - Provides layer-specific task recommendations - Explains each task before execution - Zooms to the active layer - Opens the attribute table - Displays layer name, type, CRS, source, fields and feature information - Selects all features - Clears the current selection - Creates buffers in metres or kilometres - Automatically uses a suitable metric CRS for accurate buffers - Creates Polygon centroids - Extracts Line vertices - Repairs invalid geometries - Adds geometry information - Displays Raster layer details - Applies Raster contrast enhancement - Creates temporary outputs without modifying the original data - Maintains a list of generated results - Removes selected generated results - Includes Point, Line and Polygon sample datasets - Includes built-in Help and compatibility Self-check - Displays task activity and error messages - Requires no account, internet connection, terminal setup or external Python packages
GeoFlow Guide is developed by Hrishikesh Tambe and Ballu Harish under the RRI Skill and Knowledge Foundation.
Source code and issue reporting: https://github.com/rrisk4all/geoflow-guide

pyqgis_plugin.name: Cadence Connector
pyqgis_plugin.description: This plugin connects QGIS to Cadence allowing users to upload files and styling to projects and maps in Cadence.
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin connects QGIS and Cadence, City Science's flagship cloud-based GIS product. The plugin allows users to send their files and styling from QGIS to a Cadence project and/or maps.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Inpaint AI Cloud
pyqgis_plugin.description: Bilingual cloud AI inpainting for orthophotos in QGIS using OpenAI Image Edit
pyqgis_plugin.about: Bilingual PL/EN cloud inpainting workflow specialized for realistic orthophoto editing. Requires an OpenAI API account, API key, internet access and QGIS Authentication Manager. Image crops, masks and prompts are sent to the external OpenAI Image Edit service only after user consent.

pyqgis_plugin.name: KICT SWAT-K 2026
pyqgis_plugin.description: KICT SWAT-K 2026
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin is designed to convert and view SWAT output (RCH) files.

pyqgis_plugin.name: NISAR Processor
pyqgis_plugin.description: QGIS toolbox for NISAR Level-2 GCOV product inspection, scientific raster extraction, visualization, quality layers, and analysis-ready raster export. Requirement - GDAL 3.13 or newer.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Work with NISAR Level-2 GCOV products: inspect datasets, validate dataset-level georeferencing, extract scientific rasters, export Float32 GeoTIFFs, visualize SAR data, and create dual-pol RGB composites. Source HDF5 values are preserved and the original product is never modified. Requirement - GDAL 3.13 or newer.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Deepak Kumar, Ashutosh Singh, Rahul Jayprakash Sharma

pyqgis_plugin.name: SeaState US
pyqgis_plugin.description: Load U.S. NOAA coastal observations — tide-gauge water levels, tide predictions, and offshore buoys — as time-aware QGIS layers.
pyqgis_plugin.about: SeaState US pulls data from NOAA CO-OPS (Tides & Currents tide-gauge stations) and the National Data Buoy Center (NDBC offshore buoys) into QGIS as styled point layers, and charts any layer as a time series. Coverage is U.S. coasts, the Great Lakes, and territories. Uses keyless public APIs — no account required.

pyqgis_plugin.name: YAAP(Yet Another Animation Plugin)
pyqgis_plugin.description: Turn QGIS into a video editing software
pyqgis_plugin.about:
YAAP(Yet Another Animation Plugin) is a QGIS plugin that expand the capabilities of the temporal controller and the expression engine to create beautiful animation in QGIS.
Enhances your methodologies with animations, make data visualisation, educational video, or even art with it
This plugin was created while creating these videos: * https://lnkd.in/p/eJGA25DA * https://youtu.be/VqZFsCQ5UJ4 * https://youtu.be/R6kVB-uChUg
Introduction to animation in QGIS presented at Laax user conference: https://talks.osgeo.org/qgis-uc2026/talk/MNDQQH/

pyqgis_plugin.name: Repoliner - репозитории модулей
pyqgis_plugin.description: Builds a QGIS plugin repository (plugins.xml) from ready-made plugin archives. Собирает репозиторий модулей QGIS (plugins.xml) из готовых архивов модулей.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Select plugin zip archives, and Repoliner reads metadata.txt from each of them and writes plugins.xml in the format of the QGIS plugin repository. Several repositories are kept at once, each with its own set of plugins. For every plugin the window shows whether its archive is in place and whether the archive version matches the registry. The registry address is copied in the file:/// form and added in Plugins - Manage and Install Plugins - Settings. Developed by Inform++ LLC (www.informpp.ru). . Выбираются zip-архивы модулей, Repoliner читает metadata.txt каждого из них и записывает plugins.xml в формате репозитория модулей QGIS. Окно держит несколько репозиториев, в каждом свой набор модулей. У каждого модуля видно, на месте ли архив и совпадает ли его версия с реестром. Адрес реестра копируется в виде file:/// и добавляется в Модули - Управление и установка модулей - Настройки. Разработано ООО «Информ++» (www.informpp.ru).

pyqgis_plugin.name: StereonetStudio
pyqgis_plugin.description: Professional stereographic projection (stereonet): polar/equatorial grid, poles, density contours, rose diagram, kinematic analysis (planar slide, wedge slide, flexural and direct toppling), with import from CSV/TXT files or project vector layers, plus local structural/topographic orientation acquisition from DTM rasters by mouse click. User interface fully translated (Italian/English).
pyqgis_plugin.about: StereonetStudio draws a stereographic projection (equal-angle / equal-area, lower/upper hemisphere, polar or equatorial grid) starting from structural data (dip/dip direction, strike/dip, trend/plunge), imported from CSV/TXT files or directly from vector layers loaded into the project (with automatic field selection in the menus). Modern tabbed interface (Stereonet, Data, Kinematic Analysis, Rosette), fully translated into Italian and English, with comprehensive options for labels, line weights, colors, poles, density contours (poles, intersections, data column; solid or line style, with fill extending to the great circle boundary), rose diagram of directions, and a complete kinematic analysis module (planar slide, wedge slide, flexural toppling, direct toppling) with envelopes, friction cones, lateral limits, and highlighted zones. The legend and density scale (both in bold, with configurable text size for title/legend/items) are positioned in the top left corner, right below the title which is always fully visible. The panel opens as a pre-resized window and stays on top until closed. Includes a dedicated DTM acquisition module with automatic selection of project DTM rasters, local-plane least-squares fitting, configurable sampling radius (1–15 cells), direct map-click acquisition, automatic calculation of Dip, Dip Direction, Strike, Pole Trend/Plunge, and X/Y/Z coordinates. Quality control includes cell count, RMSE, maximum residual, configurable RMSE threshold, optional rejection of measurements exceeding the threshold, and map highlighting of the fitting window. Multiple measurements can be acquired continuously, with a complete structural/topographic table, progressive IDs, Set/Group fields, and export file CSV, Geopakage and Shapefile. Valid measurements are automatically transferred to the Data tab, while preserving its existing format logic. DTM acquisition and UI logic are kept modular in separate components.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QNEAT
pyqgis_plugin.description: QNEAT - QGIS Network Analysis Toolbox
pyqgis_plugin.about: The QNEAT (short for QGIS Network Analysis Toolbox) Plugin aims to provide sophisticated QGIS Processing-Toolbox algorithms in the field of network analysis. QNEAT is integrated in the QGIS Processing Framework. It offers algorithms that range from simple shortest path solving to more complex tasks like Iso-Area (aka service areas, accessibility polygons) and OD-Matrix (Origin-Destination-Matrix) computation.
pyqgis_plugin.tags: network analysis,graph analysis,od matrix,distance matrix,od matrices,od,isochrone areas,catchment areas,shortest path,dijkstra

pyqgis_plugin.name: Eurekarto SVG Tools
pyqgis_plugin.description: Export a print layout map frame to a grouped, named SVG for Illustrator or Inkscape.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Created by Blanche Lambert for Eurêkarto in 2026. Writes a map frame to one SVG file with a group per layer, a group per symbology class and a named group per feature, polygons optionally joined on an identifier field such as an ISO code. English and French interfaces. Copyright © 2026 Blanche Lambert / Eurêkarto. GNU GPL v2 or later.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Eurekarto Projection Tools
pyqgis_plugin.description: Cut vector layers where a projection tears, clip them to its horizon, and build projection outlines.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Created by Blanche Lambert for Eurêkarto in 2026. Includes Antimeridian Cutter, Auto Cutter, Horizon Cutter and grid-based Projection Outline, with English and French interfaces. Copyright © 2026 Blanche Lambert / Eurêkarto. GNU GPL v2 or later.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Flutwellen
pyqgis_plugin.description: https://github.com/RetepRelleum/flutwelle
pyqgis_plugin.about: Simplified procedure for calculating a flood wave with primarily one-dimensional propagation. This program is used to estimate the flood wave. The user is responsible for verifying the results. The user is responsible for any consequences. In addition to activating the plug-in, the GeoTIF files of the region to be examined must be downloaded to a directory. The files can be found at swissALTI3D or swissSURFACE3D, but it is preferable to store them in separate folders.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Wake
pyqgis_plugin.description: Watch live marine vessel traffic (AIS) on your map — stream ships in your map view or a drawn area.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Wake streams live AIS vessel positions into QGIS and shows them moving on the map — track your current map view or draw an area to watch. Choose a data source: aisstream.io (global, free account and API key), Open Waters/aiscast (free token), or Digitraffic (Finland/Baltic, no key). Vessels are coloured by type and rotated by heading, with name, flag, speed and destination; busy areas cluster into counted badges, and a toggle shows only moving vessels. Built on a provider abstraction so other AIS sources can be added. Data is live only — Wake does not replay history.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Coastal Inundation Under Climate Change
pyqgis_plugin.description: Sea level rise flood mapping with hydraulic connectivity and DEM uncertainty bands
pyqgis_plugin.about: Plugin created by Daniel Ibarra Marinas, Facultad de Ingeniería y Ciencias, Universidad Autónoma de Tamaulipas. Floods only what lies below the new sea level and connects to the sea. Uncertainty bands from DEM RMSE and projection sigma, classified disconnected low areas, styled GeoTIFF and GeoPackage outputs, statistics and metadata. Static model: no erosion, waves or drainage. Interface in English and Spanish.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Daniel Ibarra Marinas, Facultad de Ingeniería y Ciencias, Universidad Autónoma de Tamaulipas

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoVisual Lineament — Experimental Validation v7.2.3
pyqgis_plugin.description: Experimental validation build for DEM-derived lineament extraction with A0-A5 ablation of Continuity-Gated Evidence Refinement (CGER).
pyqgis_plugin.about: Preserves the v7.1 scientific detection core and adds a reproducible A0-A5 experimental validation framework from a common intermediate candidate set, candidate-level decision audit, validation metrics, manifest hashes, and MIN_AZ=2 sensitivity output. Outputs remain DEM-derived lineament candidates and require geological validation.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Agus Santoso Budiharso (developed with AI assistance)

pyqgis_plugin.name: Base de dados GeoMaringá
pyqgis_plugin.description: Access the data collection of the municipality of Maringá, Paraná, Brazil, directly through QGIS. (Acesse o acervo de dados da prefeitura do município de Maringá diretamente pelo QGIS.)
pyqgis_plugin.about: Access the data collection of the municipality of Maringá, Paraná, Brazil, directly through QGIS. The plugin requests data from the GeoMaringá portal and adds the desired layer to QGIS. (Acesse o acervo de dados da prefeitura do município de Maringá diretamente pelo QGIS. O plugin faz uma requisição aos dados do portal GeoMaringá e adiciona a camada desejada ao QGIS.)

pyqgis_plugin.name: Recalculo RTK a Coordenadas Ajustadas
pyqgis_plugin.description: Recalculates field points collected against a "free" RTK base to the base's adjusted coordinates from static GNSS post-processing (plane and geographic).
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Surveying and cadastral plugin for GNSS/RTK work. From the coordinates of a "free" RTK base taken in the field and its adjusted coordinates (obtained by static GNSS post-processing), it computes the translation vector and applies it to every point in a comma-delimited CSV file, letting you choose the X/Easting, Y/Northing and Z/elevation columns. It recalculates both projected (plane) and geographic (longitude/latitude) coordinates, adds the resulting points as a layer to the project, can also export them to Shapefile (.shp) and DXF (.dxf), and can optionally generate an HTML technical report of the recalculation. The interface and the technical report are available in Spanish, English and Brazilian Portuguese, detected automatically from QGIS's own interface language.
Complemento de topografia y catastro para GNSS/RTK. A partir de la coordenada de la base tomada libre en campo y su coordenada ajustada (obtenida por postproceso estatico), calcula el vector de traslacion y lo aplica a todos los puntos de un archivo CSV (delimitado por comas), permitiendo elegir las columnas de X/Este, Y/Norte y Z/elevacion. Recalcula tanto las coordenadas planas (proyectadas) como las geograficas (longitud/latitud), agrega los puntos resultantes como capa al proyecto, permite exportarlos tambien a Shapefile (.shp) y a DXF (.dxf), y puede generar opcionalmente un reporte tecnico en HTML del recalculo. La interfaz y el reporte tecnico estan disponibles en espanol, ingles y portugues de Brasil, detectados automaticamente segun el idioma configurado en QGIS.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Contrail
pyqgis_plugin.description: Watch live aircraft traffic (ADS-B) on your map — stream planes in your map view or a drawn area.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Contrail streams live ADS-B aircraft positions into QGIS and shows them moving on the map — track your current map view or draw an area to watch. Choose a data source: adsb.lol, adsb.fi, or the OpenSky Network — all free and keyless, no account required. Aircraft are coloured by category and rotated to their track, with callsign, country, altitude, speed and squawk; busy areas cluster into counted badges, a toggle shows only airborne aircraft, and emergency squawks (7500/7600/7700) are highlighted. Built on a provider abstraction so other ADS-B sources can be added. Data is live only — Contrail does not replay history. It is the sky-side companion to Wake, which does the same for live marine vessel traffic.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Zenith
pyqgis_plugin.description: Watch live satellites overhead on your map — computed from orbital data, in your map view or a drawn area.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Zenith streams live satellite positions into QGIS and shows them moving on the map — track your current map view or draw an area to watch. Satellites don't broadcast their positions, so Zenith fetches their orbital elements (TLEs) free and keyless from CelesTrak and computes each satellite's position locally with SGP4 — which means no rate limits and complete global coverage. Pick a group: space stations (ISS), the brightest/visible satellites, the GPS constellation, weather satellites, Starlink, or all active satellites. Satellites are coloured by constellation/type, busy areas cluster into counted badges, and clicking a satellite opens it on N2YO. Data is live only — Zenith does not replay history. It is the space-side companion to Wake (marine vessels) and Contrail (aircraft). Uses the vendored pure-Python sgp4 library (Brandon Rhodes, MIT).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Cell Grid Creator
pyqgis_plugin.description: Creates standardized geographic grids for a selected AOI in QGIS, with automatic alignment, cell extraction, and cell ID generation across resolutions from 1° to 1′.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Cell Grid Creator is a QGIS plugin for creating standardized geographic grid cells within a selected AOI. Users can select the required grid scale, browse supported AOI formats, and generate the corresponding grid automatically. The plugin creates cell identifiers, coordinates, codes, export information, and cell names, and saves the generated grid as an ESRI Shapefile in a CELL_GRID output folder.

pyqgis_plugin.name: USGS Planetary Analysis Ready Data Search Tool
pyqgis_plugin.description: Search the USGS Astrogeology Planetary Analysis Ready Data STAC API by target, collection, assets, extent, dates, and item-level queryables.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Provides cascading target, collection, asset, and queryable controls for searching the USGS Astrogeology STAC API. Results can be written to a GeoPackage and COG assets can optionally be loaded into QGIS.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Routeliner
pyqgis_plugin.description: Route events and CIS chainage (pikets): point and line events, ledger with station equations, reverse locating, longitudinal profiles
pyqgis_plugin.about: Linear referencing for QGIS with full support of CIS chainage practice: station formats (ПК 15+35, км+м, railway km/picket), picket ledgers with station equations (forward and backward), several chainage systems per route. Routes are assembled from shuffled multipart pieces and true arcs. Every run reports unplaced records with the reason. Routes carry chainage in M values: read from the geometry, calibrated from a ledger or control points, and written into results for PostGIS and ArcGIS. Longitudinal profiles sample rasters at pickets and events and draw a profile grid with grades and a straightened plan for print layouts. Includes a demo generator with analytically computed reference answers. Pure PyQGIS + NumPy, no external dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: IMI Rates Portugal (flatin.pt)
pyqgis_plugin.description: Adds a map layer with the yearly IMI (municipal property tax) rate of all 308 municipalities of Portugal, styled by rate, with official boundaries.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Adds one layer: the yearly urban IMI rate (Imposto Municipal sobre Imóveis) of every municipality of Portugal, on official municipal boundaries, coloured by rate. Choose the latest verified tax year or an earlier one.
Coverage: Portugal only (mainland, Madeira and the Azores).
Requirements: an internet connection to https://flatin.pt when the layer is added. No account, no key, no extra Python packages. The plugin sends no telemetry; it contacts flatin.pt only when you open its dialog (to list the tax years) and when you add the layer.
Data: the rates are checked against the Autoridade Tributária portal and published by flatin.pt as open data under CC BY 4.0 (https://flatin.pt/en/tools/imi-open-data/). Where a municipality sets its rate per parish, the rate is empty, never zero. Boundaries: Carta Administrativa Oficial de Portugal (CAOP), Direção-Geral do Território, CC BY 4.0, simplified for mapping. Credits are kept in the layer metadata.
flatin.pt is not a real estate agency.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Velorona
pyqgis_plugin.description: Telecom link evidence, inside QGIS. Explore -> Select -> Analyze -> Evidence -> Export.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Velorona for QGIS -- Telecom link evidence, inside QGIS. 1. Explore -- Load public telecom infrastructure and your own data. 2. Select -- Choose a site, link, or two endpoints. 3. Analyze -- Run path clearance, microwave weather exposure, or satellite geometry. 4. Evidence -- See what is observed, what is calculated, and what is inferred. 5. Export -- Take the evidence with you as a structured CSV/GeoJSON result. Three analysis engines, all reused unmodified: Terrestrial Path Clearance (aei_link_clearance), Microwave Weather Exposure (aei_mw_exposure), Satellite/Earth-Space look angles (skyfield/SGP4). Requires aei-microwave-link-exposure, aei-link-clearance, aei-geo-features, and skyfield to be installed in QGIS's own Python environment.

pyqgis_plugin.name: go3streetview
pyqgis_plugin.description: a plugin for Google Street View© interaction within QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about: go3streetview allows to get a Google Street View frame clicking and dragging the cursor on map to set location and direction of the desired view. Features: Automatic SRS conversion, Transparent proxying, View position on map, Take Snapshots of current view, Dockable Dialog Windows, Overlay info layer support, Map follows Streetview, Streetview service coverage, Digitize on Street View
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: César Benjamín (based on work of Enrico Ferreguti)

pyqgis_plugin.name: Overlap Analyzer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Analyzes the spatial overlap between selected layers and a reference layer, optionally including a buffer zone. Lists intersecting features with their attribute table.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Overlap Analyzer analyzes the spatial intersections between the selected layers and a reference layer, and presents the results in a table. Compatible with Qt5 and Qt6.

pyqgis_plugin.name: qgSurf
pyqgis_plugin.description: Processing of geological planes and surfaces
pyqgis_plugin.about: qgSurf is a field-mapping/structural-geology plugin that can be used as an aid in: a) estimating the attitude of sub-planar geological surfaces given three or more points on a topographic surface; b) determining the intersection between a geological plane and a topographic surface; c) calculating the distance between points and a geological plane; d) plotting geological data in a stereonet; e) creating geological profiles; f) interpreting exported geological profiles in an editable distance-elevation section plane.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Contour plugin
pyqgis_plugin.description: Generates contours from point layer
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Generate a contour layer based on an attribute of a point vector layer.
Builds a processing plugin and a GUI interface for simple direct contouring of point layers. The source point layer Can be either gridded or randomly organised. The layer resulting contours can be rendered with a graduated renderer using a colour ramp. The layer includes properties that can be used to replicate or modify the contouring parameters.
Requires python modules numpy and matplotlib
Recommends loading the MemoryLayerSaver plugin to save the contours with the project

pyqgis_plugin.name: PostGIS Topology Editor

pyqgis_plugin.about: Editing toolbar for PostGIS topology primitives (ISO SQL/MM based)

pyqgis_plugin.name: qProf
pyqgis_plugin.description: Calculates height and slope profiles from DEM and GPX files, and plots geological attitudes and traces on profiles.
pyqgis_plugin.about: qProf is a plugin for the generation of topographic and geological profiles. Topography can be extracted from DEM or GPX files. Geological data, such as stratification attitude and geological traces, can be projected on the profile. Intersections between geological outcrops or faults can be determined.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Pic2Map
pyqgis_plugin.description: Compute the 3D orientation of a picture and provide the interaction between the picture and the map.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Pic2map has two goals. First, it is used to compute the location and orientation of a picture with 3D Ground Control Points. The orientation can be saved in a Google Earth format. Second, it provides the interaction between the map and the picture through a Digital Elevation Model. Vector layers can be overlaid on the picture, geographic vector layer can be digitized directly in the picture, the picture can be "orthorectified".
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Gillian Milani, Timothée Produit, Frédérick Pineault, Johary Rakotomalala, Raphaël David

pyqgis_plugin.name: OpenQuake Integrated Risk Modelling Toolkit

pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin allows users to drive OpenQuake Engine calculations (https://github.com/gem/oq-engine) of physical hazard and risk, and to load the corresponding outputs as QGIS layers. For those outputs, data visualization tools are provided.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Isogeo
