pyqgis_plugin.name: Get WKT
pyqgis_plugin.description: This plugin displays the selected features' WKT, EWKT or JSON representation.
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin displays the selected features' WKT, EWKT or JSON representation. It differs from QGIS's Core copy functionality by only extracting the features WKT, rather than the entire record. Simply select a feature, press the button and the WKT, EWKT or JSON represenation will be displayed in a dialog box where you can copy its content for use in creating or updating geometries in SQL statements. Based on the original version for QGIS 2 by Hugo Ledoux at https://github.com/hugoledoux/QGIS-getWKT

pyqgis_plugin.name: Swiss Locator

pyqgis_plugin.name: Model Baker

pyqgis_plugin.about: Model Baker (previously QgsProjectGenerator) creates QGIS projects from INTERLIS models, PostGIS database schemas or GeoPackages. It preconfigures layers, widgets, relations and much more based on meta information available from models.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Trajectools
pyqgis_plugin.description: Processing tools for handling trajectory data
pyqgis_plugin.about: Trajectools adds trajectory analysis algorithms to the QGIS Processing toolbox. Trajectools requires MovingPandas >= 0.22.3 and optionally integrates scikit-mobility (for privacy tests), stonesoup (for smoothing), and gtfs_functions (for GTFS data support). See the plugin homepage for installation recommendations. Sample data for testing the functionality is provided with the plugin download.

pyqgis_plugin.name: RasterTimeseriesManager
pyqgis_plugin.description: Explore and visualizing spatio-spectral-temporal Earth Observation imagery data.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The Raster Timeseries Manager plugin adds a dock panel with time controls that allow to smoothly navigate through earth observation imagery data like Landsat, Sentinel and Modis and derived products in the temporal domain. Layer styling and spatial navigation is handled by QGIS as usual. See the project homepage for a detailed overview and usage instructions.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Andreas Rabe (Geomatics Lab, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Germany)

pyqgis_plugin.name: WaterNetAnalyzer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Generate water network, get flow path upstream/downstream
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin creates a network with one outlet from a line layer (shapefile). A warning is generated when circles are found in the network. You can use the tools to show the flow path upstream or downstream of a segment in the network and accumulate flow/loads along the flow path. An instructional video can be found here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3GBr57evQPI (thanks to Hans van der Kwast). First versions of this plugin have been developed within the project PROSPER-RO, funded by BMBF, grant number 033L212. pyqgis_plugin.name: D.E.M. Slicer

pyqgis_plugin.about: It is a simple tool for cutting (in slices) of DEM, to draw pretty postcards, for the lovers of reliefs.

pyqgis_plugin.name: OSM Data Sync
pyqgis_plugin.description: Maintain an own local dataset whith local attributes while keeping it in sync with OpenStreetMap (OSM)
pyqgis_plugin.about:
This plugin allows a user to maintain an own local spatial vector dataset, which is strongly related to OpenStreetMap (OSM), while keeping it in sync with OSM. The dataset is being defined as an Overpass query and the dataset can contain additional, local features and features can contain additional attributes.
The plugin has two main functions:
• Iterate forth and back through the features of the layer (similar to Go2NextFeature). • Synchronize the local dataset with OSM data on user demand, which means, that it flags updated and deleted features and that it downloads new features.
The plugin requires a simple configuration (.osmds) which is a sidecar file to the local dataset (e.g. a GeoPackage) and uses an Overpass API to retrieve the OSM data.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Christopher Hilfing, Hanna Wildermuth, Stefan Keller

pyqgis_plugin.name: Go2NextFeaturePlus
pyqgis_plugin.description: Allows jumping from a feature to another following an attribute order
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin allows to select a layer and jump from a feature to the next. It is possible to select an attribute of the layer (e.g. name) which defines the ordering. Besides the Pan function there's a Pan and Zoom function for polygons and lines and other options. In addition to the mentioned functionality it is also possible to set and persist a state ("fixed", "already fixed", "no issue", "unknown" or "undefined") of each feature. For this the layer needs to be updatable (which excludes e.g. formats like CSV or GeoJSON which need to be converted e.g. to GeoPackage).
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Diego Fantino, Christopher Hilfing, Hanna Wildermuth, Stefan Keller, Alberto De Luca (for Tabacco Editrice)

pyqgis_plugin.name: Generate SWMM inp
pyqgis_plugin.description: Generate SWMM input files from layers, import input files from SWMM to QGIS and import SWMM report files to QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about:
This plugin provides tools to generate SWMM input files from layers in QGIS, and to import SWMM input files into QGIS. You can create submodels above or below a certain node in your model layers. The plugin needs the python library 'pandas' which should be included in current QGIS versions. If it is not already installed, it can be added in a advanced QGIS installation or via pip. Instructions and a documentation can be found on the plugin´s GIT (see link "homepage" below).
Cite as: Schilling, J.; Tränckner, J. Generate_SWMM_inp: An Open-Source QGIS Plugin to Import and Export Model Input Files for SWMM. Water 2022, 14, 2262. https://doi.org/10.3390/w14142262
First versions (0.1 to 0.31) of this plugin have been developed within the project PROSPER-RO, funded by BMBF, grant number 033L212. New features and bugfixes (versions 0.32 to 0.39) have been added within the project OSWeGe, funded by BMUV, grant number 67DAS263

pyqgis_plugin.name: Mesh Tools

pyqgis_plugin.about: Tools for for management of Data using Mesh format : - Culvert Manager - Sources Manager - Mesh Quality Analysis Developed by Aurélien Perrin (Artelia), Nicolas Godet (ISL), and Christophe Coulet (BRGM)

pyqgis_plugin.name: Marine Tools
pyqgis_plugin.description: Tools for marine habitat mapping
pyqgis_plugin.about: Marine tools for analysis and interpretation (Now for QGIS versions 3&4). These tools include: Benthic Terrain Modeller - geomorphological interpretation of bathymetry data, OBIA - Object Based Image Analysis using a simple k-means algorithm, MBES Segmentation - Classification using OBIA on bathymetry and backscatter data from a Multibeam Echosounder, Bathymetry Morphometry - Create several derivatives from bathymetry data, Spike filter (deviation filter from median), Tools for multibeam survey design (new surveys and filling in surveys), Imagery manipulation - removing outliers and changing null settings, Grey level Co-occurrence Matrices (GLCM), CSV conversion to points or grids, Information listing of all Layers in project, Random Forest predictions (using R), CoMMa feature delineation, Sidescan sonar synthetic imagery, Txt navigation files to line + some test data. Now fully documented.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Tim Le Bas, National Oceanography Centre, Southampton. UK.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Mineral Exploration Web Services

pyqgis_plugin.name: AIAMAS - AI-Assisted Map Styler
pyqgis_plugin.description: Symbolize your vector layers in seconds
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin allows quick symbolization and automatically suggests fitting colors and symbols for newly loaded vector layers. It does not replace the QGIS Style Manager. Vector layer names are assigned to the most similar entity name (e.g. bank, restaurant) using a list of predefined entities with associated styles. The suggested styles - i.e. colors and symbols - can be applied as is, or customized with a few mouse clicks. To match layer names to entity names a Large Language Model (LLM) is used for semantic similarity. If no LLM service is available, the plugin defaults to algorithmic string similarity methods. The plugin uses an open source LLM service hosted by the Institute for Software (IFS) at the Eastern Switzerland University of Applied Sciences (OST). To use this plugin, an API token must be entered in the Options dialog. This token can be generated for free on the IFS LLMHub website https://llmhub.infs.ch/. By using this service, you agree to follow its policy. The plugin primarily handles layer names in English, German and French. Help improve this plugin. Submit an issue or a merge request.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Diego Fantino, Niklas Vogel, Samuel Meuli, Stefan Keller

pyqgis_plugin.name: SEILAPLAN
pyqgis_plugin.description: Seillinien-Layoutplaner — A cable road layout planner
pyqgis_plugin.about:
[DE] SEILAPLAN ermöglicht die einfache und effiziente Planung von Seillinien unter Berücksichtigung topografischer Gegebenheiten. Die implementierte Berechnungsmethode basiert auf der Methode von Zweifel (1960) und beschreibt die Kettenlinie, unter Annahme einer beidseitig fixierten Verankerung des Tragseils. Dieses QGIS-Plugin ist ein Hilfsmittel. Jede Lösung muss vor Umsetzung durch eine geschulte Fachperson geprüft werden. Jegliche Haftung wird im Rahmen der GNU General Public Licence Version 2 oder neuere ausgeschlossen (www.gnu.org/licenses).
***
[EN] SEILAPLAN enables simple and efficient planning of cable roads, taking topographical conditions into account. The implemented calculation method is based on the method developed by Zweifel (1960) and describes the catenary, assuming that the skyline is anchored at both ends. This QGIS plugin is a tool. Every solution must be checked by a trained specialist before implementation. Any liability is excluded under the GNU General Public License Version 2 or later (www.gnu.org/licenses).
***
Dokumentation: https://seilaplan.wsl.ch
***
Bont, Moll, Ramstein, Frutig, Heinimann, Schweier (2022). Introducing Seilaplan, a QGIS plugin for cable road layout planning. Croatian Journal of Forest Engineering, 2022. https://doi.org/10.5552/crojfe.2022.1824

pyqgis_plugin.about:
Plugin ma 2 funkcie - 1. stahuje kataster do GPKG / 2. otvori kataster v prehliadaci podla aktualnych suradnic v QGIS staci zadat nazov alebo kod KÚ a stiahne vrstvy podla vyberu, pripadne transformuje do 5514 - ulozi GPKG do zvoleneho adresara presnost sub 1 cm (tak ako INSPIRE GML, zdroj je EPSG 4326) stahuje z INSPIRE OGC API, ktore je podla VÚGK v overovacej prevadzke a preto je plugin v sekcii experimentalne
ak by chcel niekto ine styly na stiahnute vrstvy staci prepisat qml subory v adresari pluginu svojimi vlastnymi
NOVINKA v0.15: Pokus o opravu stahovania (najma vacsich miest, ktorym predtym nestiahlo vrstvu ParcelC) - nahradena logika priestorovym delenim (mriezka 4x4), eliminuju sa timeouty servera pri velkych offsetoch. Pribudli priebezne aktualizacie progresu pocas stahovania.
Za data dakujeme: © VÚGK (Výskumný ústav geodézie a kartografie v Bratislave), INSPIRE ukladacie služby
NOVINKA v0.13: Moznost stiahnut cely okres alebo kraj naraz - vhodne najma pre CadastralUnit. Dalej rezim vytvorenia hromadneho GPKG a suvisiaci filter podla nazvu alebo kodu katastralneho uzemia. Pozor! - po stiahnuti uzemia, ktore uz v hromadnom subore je, sa toto prepise.
NOVINKA v0.12: Plugin uz obsahuje vlastnu transformaciu EPSG:4326 -> EPSG:5514 s oficialnou SK GKU transformaciou a grid suborom. Transformacia funguje automaticky pri zaznaceni "Transform to EPSG:5514" - nie je potrebne nastavovat v QGIS manualne!

pyqgis_plugin.name: ArchaeoTrace
pyqgis_plugin.description: Local-first contour tracing for historical maps with optional AI assistance and experimental DEM reconstruction.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
ArchaeoTrace helps users digitize elevation contours from scanned historical maps and review locally generated terrain hypotheses.
Features: - Multi-scale 9/15/31px Ink Centerline with a bounded 320px direction-aware Live-Wire - Literal 0-100% cursor/path coordinate blending; green preview shows the path accepted by the next click - Optional Smart Recovery for weak Ink segments; default OFF with an explicitly installed EfficientSAM-Ti model - Freehand plus LSD, HED, MobileSAM, SAM (ViT-B), and Legacy Canny under Advanced / Legacy methods - Elevation attributes and optional spot-height capture - Experimental linear-TIN DEM and hillshade generation from saved elevation data - Developer-only reproducible benchmarks with publication ranking disabled until independent review
External dependencies: default Ink and Freehand use NumPy supplied by QGIS. SciPy and scikit-image are optional Ink optimizations. Smart Recovery requires ONNX Runtime and separately installed fixed-hash weights. LSD, HED, and SAM require OpenCV; MobileSAM and full SAM additionally require requests, PyTorch, their pinned backend package, and separately downloaded weights. Installation commands and platform notes are in the linked homepage README. QGIS 3.22/Python 3.8 remains a source and no-pip contract target; optional pip stacks require Python 3.10 or newer. See the release-readiness record for the exact locally executed and configured-but-not-run QGIS matrix.
Processing is local-first and map data is not sent to a remote inference service. Model downloads and missing-model source checks are user-initiated network actions. Terrain outputs are reviewable hypotheses rather than archaeological ground truth.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SOLWEIG
pyqgis_plugin.description: Calculate Mean Radiant Temperature & UTCI thermal comfort using the SOLWEIG model.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
SOLWEIG (Solar and Longwave Environmental Irradiance Geometry) is a high-performance urban microclimate model for calculating Mean Radiant Temperature and thermal comfort indices.
Features: - Single timestep and timeseries Tmrt calculations - UTCI (Universal Thermal Climate Index) computation - PET (Physiological Equivalent Temperature) computation - Sky View Factor (SVF) preprocessing - EPW & SUEWS weather file import - Support for large rasters via tiled processing and GPU
Requirements: - The SOLWEIG Python library must be installed separately. - The plugin will offer to install it automatically on first use. - To install manually, run this in the QGIS Python Console: import pip; pip.main(["install", "solweig", "--no-deps"])
Documentation: https://umep-dev.github.io/solweig/
This plugin provides QGIS Processing algorithms that wrap the SOLWEIG Python library. This version of Solweig is currently in testing as a proof of concept for Rust + GPU + tiled processing to handle large rasters.
Adapted from UMEP (Urban Multi-scale Environmental Predictor) by Fredrik Lindberg, Sue Grimmond, and contributors. If you use this plugin in research, please cite:
Lindberg F, Grimmond CSB, Gabey A, Huang B, Kent CW, Sun T, Theeuwes N, Järvi L, Ward H, Capel-Timms I, Chang YY, Jonsson P, Krave N, Liu D, Meyer D, Olofson F, Tan JG, Wästberg D, Xue L, Zhang Z (2018) Urban Multi-scale Environmental Predictor (UMEP) - An integrated tool for city-based climate services. Environmental Modelling and Software 99, 70-87 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2017.09.020
pyqgis_plugin.tags: urban planning,microclimate,heat stress,pet,mean radiant temperature,urban climate,utci,thermal comfort

The user can interactively change the pixel values of a classification raster using intuitive tools: - Selection: draw a selection shape over the chosen pixels using the QGIS built-in Select Feature tools to change their value. - Brush and Erase: change pixel values by dragging your mouse over them. - Polygons: convert regions of uniform classification into polygons, modify their borders with QGIS built-in tools and see the changes reflected on the raster. pyqgis_plugin.name: Netcad DNS Koordinat Donusum
pyqgis_plugin.description: Coordinate transformation using Netcad DNS files: Helmert, Affine and TIN methods.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
This plugin reads Netcad .dns transformation files and applies coordinate transformation to selected vector layers.
SUPPORTED METHODS: - Helmert (4 parameters): Isotropic scale + rotation + translation. Most common method. Minimum 2 control points required. - Affine (6 parameters): Different scale in E/N direction + shear. More flexible. Minimum 3 control points required. - TIN (Delaunay Triangulation): Local transformation per triangle. Residual = 0 at all control points (exact pass-through). Best accuracy for large areas. Minimum 3 control points required.
SUPPORTED DNS FILE TYPES: - Point-Based ($AMAT + $NOK): Parameters computed from control points via LSQ. - Matrix-Based ($AMAT only): Parameters read directly from $AMAT matrix.
QUALITY CONTROL: - Data Snooping (Baarda Test): Iteratively detects suspicious control points. - Normalized residuals (w-values) vs critical value comparison. - Error ellipses: sigma_E, sigma_N, sigma_P, semi-major/minor axes. - Residual vector and error ellipse layers can be added to the map.
MULTI-LAYER SUPPORT: - Multiple layers can be selected (Ctrl/Shift) and transformed in one step. - Option to transform in-place or create new layers with custom suffix.
REPORTING: - HTML report: Opens in browser with full CSS styling. - PDF report: Generated via QGIS WebEngine.
Compatible with QGIS 3.16+ and QGIS 4.x (Qt5/Qt6). scipy package required for TIN method.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Cityseer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Urban network analysis: centrality, demand flows, accessibility, mixed uses, and statistics
pyqgis_plugin.about: Cityseer provides Processing algorithms for urban network analysis: network centrality (closeness and betweenness), demand-weighted flow betweenness from weighted origins and destinations, land-use accessibility, mixed-use diversity, and localised statistics. Metrics are computed on a dual graph representation where each road segment is a node connected to its neighbours. All distances are network distances walked along the streets, not straight-line distances, with support for multiple distance thresholds, shortest and simplest (angular) paths, boundary polygons, and optional adaptive sampling. Requires the cityseer Python library: pip install cityseer

pyqgis_plugin.name: TRACT Geolocation Formatter
pyqgis_plugin.description: Validate, clean, and convert geolocation layers into the TRACT GeoJSON template for sustainability and traceability workflows.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The TRACT Geolocation Formatter is a QGIS plugin designed to help GIS practitioners prepare geolocation datasets for ingestion into the TRACT platform. The plugin validates and cleans polygon geometries, standardizes coordinate precision, and converts layers into the TRACT GeoJSON template format. It detects common geometry issues such as self-intersections, duplicate vertices, invalid polygons, and schema inconsistencies, while providing a validation report to help users identify and correct problematic features before upload.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Copernicus Disaster Explorer

For each event (flood, wildfire, volcano, landslide) it finds the matching Sentinel-1/2 images, downloads them with real-time progress, and loads the relevant spectral bands with appropriate false-color symbology for immediate visual analysis. Floods use dual-sensor search (SAR + optical). Requires a free Copernicus Data Space account (https://dataspace.copernicus.eu). Geographic coverage: Italy (expandable). Interface in Italian.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SIOSE2CN
pyqgis_plugin.description: Calcula P0 y Número de Curva (CN) a partir de SIOSE, pendiente e IGME para flujos de trabajo hidrológicos e hidráulicos en España Peninsular.
pyqgis_plugin.about: SIOSE2CN es un complemento de QGIS que calcula automáticamente el umbral de escorrentía (P0) y el Número de Curva (CN) a partir de coberturas del suelo SIOSE-AR, pendiente del terreno derivada de un MDT, y grupos hidrológicos obtenidos de la capa de permeabilidad del IGME (escala 1:200.000). El resultado es un raster NC_CURSO listo para su uso en modelos lluvia-escorrentía como HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS 2D u otros. Válido para España Peninsular. Soporta SIOSE-AR 2016, 2017, 2018 y 2020. La capa de permeabilidad IGME puede descargarse automáticamente, cargarse desde archivo local o conectarse mediante el servidor ArcGIS REST del IGME. Este desarrollo ha contado con la colaboración de Antonio López Espinazo, que aportó la metodología y la capa maestra de permeabilidad IGME utilizada en el cálculo.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Pedro Ivar y Hugo Alejandro Bohorquez

pyqgis_plugin.name: Alberi Monumentali Italia
pyqgis_plugin.description: Scarica e visualizza gli alberi monumentali d'Italia dal registro ufficiale MASAF
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Plugin to download Italy's monumental trees registry from the official MASAF website (Ministry of Agriculture). Supports single-region or full-Italy download, converts DMS coordinates to WGS84 decimal degrees, and saves data as Shapefile or GeoPackage with graduated symbology (size proportional to trunk circumference). Data license: Creative Commons CC BY 4.0. Plugin developed with Claude AI (Anthropic) support.
ITALIANO: Plugin per scaricare gli elenchi regionali degli alberi monumentali d'Italia dal sito del Ministero dell'agricoltura, della sovranità alimentare e delle foreste (MASAF). Permette di selezionare una o più regioni oppure tutta l'Italia, converte le coordinate DMS in gradi decimali WGS84 e salva i dati in formato Shapefile o GeoPackage con tematizzazione graduata (dimensione proporzionale alla circonferenza del fusto) ed etichette con il nome volgare della specie. Visualizzazione multi-scala: coroplete regionale per densità alberi a zoom out, punti individuali a zoom in. Dati aggiornati al nono aggiornamento dell'elenco nazionale (23/10/2025). Licenza dati: Creative Commons CC BY 4.0. Plugin sviluppato con il supporto di Claude AI (Anthropic).

pyqgis_plugin.name: INGV Seismic Explorer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Import and visualize seismic events from INGV (Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia) directly in QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about:
INGV Seismic Explorer connects to the official INGV FDSNWS web services to download earthquake events and seismic station data directly into QGIS layers.
Features: - Query seismic events by date range, magnitude, depth and geographic area - Use current map extent as search area - Automatic graduated symbology (circle size = magnitude, color = depth) - Import seismic station network (Rete Sismica Nazionale, 400+ stations) - Export results to GeoPackage, Shapefile or GeoJSON
Data source: INGV FDSNWS Event API (webservices.ingv.it) No API key required. Data is open and free.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GEDIMetrics
pyqgis_plugin.description: Download, subset and merge GEDI products (L2A/L2B/L4A V002/V003; L4C V002) into a single GeoPackage with selectable variables and filters.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GEDIMetrics downloads GEDI LiDAR data from NASA EarthData, subsets it to a user-defined area of interest, merges multiple products (L2A canopy height, L2B vertical structure, L4A aboveground biomass density, L4C waveform structural complexity index) by shot_number, and exports the result as GeoPackage or GeoParquet with user-selected variables and quality filters. Version 3 (V003) supported for L2A, L2B and L4A; L4C uses V002 until usable V003 granules are available. Compatible with QGIS 3.4 and 4.0. Related preprint: https://eartharxiv.org/repository/view/13082/

pyqgis_plugin.name: AITracer by LAD
pyqgis_plugin.description: Click any feature on a georeferenced raster and SAM2 segments it instantly. Refine with positive/negative prompts, then accept to create a vector polygon. All processing runs locally — by LAD, Sapienza University of Rome.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
AITracer by LAD brings AI-assisted raster digitization to QGIS 4.
Activate the tool, click any feature in a georeferenced raster — aerial photo, drone orthophoto, scanned plan — and the SAM2-tiny model segments it instantly as a polygon preview. Refine the result with positive or negative point prompts, adjust Douglas-Peucker simplification, then accept to add the polygon to any vector layer.
HOW IT WORKS: AITracer captures a screenshot of the current QGIS canvas and sends it to SAM2 — it does not read the original raster file. This keeps processing fast and memory-light on modest hardware. The output resolution depends on your zoom level, not the raster resolution. Features that extend beyond the canvas edge will be partially traced. The canvas is locked during a session to keep pixel-to-map coordinates consistent.
First-time setup automatically downloads a standalone Python runtime and the SAM2-tiny model weights (~160 MB). An internet connection is required for this one-time step only. All subsequent processing runs entirely on your machine; no data is ever sent to external servers.
Developed by LAD — Laboratorio di Archeologia Digitale, Sapienza University of Rome.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Julian Bogdani | LAD – Laboratorio di Archeologia Digitale, Sapienza University of Rome

pyqgis_plugin.name: Environmental Assessment Studio
pyqgis_plugin.description: Runs Google Earth Engine environmental assessments from QGIS 4.x with AOI, date-range, raster, vector, and trend-analysis outputs.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Environmental Assessment Studio is a QGIS 4.x plugin for running Google Earth Engine based environmental assessments over a user-defined area of interest and time period. It supports Land Use Land Cover, Change Detection, Land Surface Temperature, LST-based Urban Heat Island with atmospheric-temperature interpretation context, Flood Analysis, NDVI, NDWI, Land Degradation, Drought, Soil Organic Carbon, Wind Direction, Carbon Emission (Biomass), Anthropogenic Emission, Carbon Sequestration, Solar Radiation, Rainfall / Precipitation Anomaly, Soil Moisture, Erosion Risk, Terrain Susceptibility to Erosion and Instability, Wildfire Risk, Air Quality, Habitat Fragmentation, and Groundwater Recharge / Runoff Potential. Outputs include styled rasters, optional processed Sentinel/Landsat stacks, optional vector layers, class-area summary tables, metadata sidecar files, and trend-analysis exports.
pyqgis_plugin.tags: change detection,qgis4,wildfire,flood,environmental assessment,ndvi,soil moisture,soil carbon,lulc,google earth engine,air quality,lst,ndwi,urban heat island,air temperature,eas,surface urban heat island,suhi

pyqgis_plugin.name: GPX_Appender
pyqgis_plugin.description: Append GPX waypoints or tracks directly into existing project layers. Drag & drop GPX files or folders, pick a destination layer, configure field mappings, and go.
pyqgis_plugin.about: For appending gpx data to already existing layers.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Districts Modeler
pyqgis_plugin.description: GIS-based district energy modeler for preparing, managing and visualising data for dynamic simulation in IDA Districts.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Districts Modeler is a free QGIS plugin developed by EQUA for creating, managing and preparing map-based models of district energy systems for simulation with IDA Districts, EQUA’s district energy simulation software. Districts Modeler and IDA Districts are products of EQUA. The plugin is free to use; detailed dynamic simulation is carried out in IDA Districts.
The Districts Modeler helps users build digital representations of district heating, district cooling and low-temperature energy networks by combining buildings, pipes, substations, energy plants, storage systems and consumers in one GIS-based environment. The plugin makes it easier to understand how a thermal energy network is structured, how different components are connected and how system data can be prepared for further analysis. Districts Modeler supports the preparation of consistent, simulation-ready models by providing tools for spatial data processing, network topology generation, data management, validation and visualisation directly in QGIS. Model data is stored in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database and can be exchanged with IDA Districts for detailed dynamic simulation.
Districts Modeler supports the preparation of consistent, simulation-ready models by providing tools for spatial data processing, network topology generation, data management, validation and visualisation directly in QGIS. Model data is stored in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database and can be exchanged with IDA Districts for detailed dynamic simulation.
The physical simulation itself is performed in IDA Districts, where users can analyse thermal and hydraulic network behaviour, building energy demand, energy sources, storage systems, control strategies and system performance over time.
Typical applications include district heating and cooling planning, network modelling, transformation studies, analysis of existing infrastructure, preparation of low-temperature or bidirectional network concepts, integration of renewable energy sources and support for research and planning projects.
Districts Modeler is intended for engineers, utilities, planners, municipalities, researchers and other stakeholders who want to prepare transparent and simulation-ready district energy models for use with IDA Districts.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GoPilot
pyqgis_plugin.description: Run cloud-based geospatial analysis and satellite workflows from Rasid.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Run cloud-based geospatial analysis and satellite processing workflows from Rasid directly within QGIS, enabling users to access advanced remote sensing tools without local computation. Fetch imagery from well-known satellite providers such as Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Mapbox, and Planet, or use your own data. Select your area of interest and apply AI-powered models for tasks including cloud detection, wheat detection, banana field monitoring, and scene parsing. The plugin simplifies complex workflows into an easy-to-use interface, allowing users to quickly generate insights, maps, and ready-to-use geospatial outputs.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS Agent Notes
pyqgis_plugin.description: Export lightweight QGIS project context as Markdown and an AI-readable manifest.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS Agent Notes exports the current QGIS project into a lightweight context folder for people and AI agents. It creates Markdown project notes, layer cards, reports, prompt files, a map snapshot, and agent_manifest.json. It does not copy, repair, package, or convert source data.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS Deliverable Inspector
pyqgis_plugin.description: Inspect QGIS projects for delivery risks and write read-only Markdown and JSON reports.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS Deliverable Inspector checks QGIS project context for common delivery risks, including missing paths, invalid layers, empty layers, mixed CRS, temporary layers, missing styles, and unsupported data sources. It reports risks only and never modifies the project or source data.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS Project Handoff
pyqgis_plugin.description: Create conservative QGIS project handoff folders and ZIP packages from local file-backed data sources.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS Project Handoff copies safe local file-backed project data into a handoff folder, records unsupported sources as risks, writes a handoff manifest and Markdown report, and creates a ZIP package for delivery. It does not convert ArcGIS projects or repair source data.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Google Earth Engine Extractor
pyqgis_plugin.description: Extract Google Earth Engine datasets (Sentinel-2, Landsat, SRTM, MODIS NDVI, Global Forest Change) directly into QGIS by vector layer extent.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Google Earth Engine Extractor lets you query and download Google Earth Engine rasters directly into QGIS from any vector layer bounding box. Supports Sentinel-2 SR, Landsat 8/9 SR, SRTM DEM, MODIS NDVI and Global Forest Change. Cloud filtering and median compositing applied automatically. Authentication via Application Default Credentials or service account JSON key. Compatible with QGIS 3.16 and above including QGIS 4.x. Requires the earthengine-api Python package (pip install earthengine-api) and a Google Earth Engine account.

pyqgis_plugin.name: River Slope Calculator
pyqgis_plugin.description: Calculate river reach slope from a DEM using Average Slope or Equal Area Slope. Output unit selectable: m/m or %.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
River Slope Calculator computes the slope of each river reach feature (line or multiline) from an underlying DEM raster, supporting two methods:
1. Average Slope (Mean Gradient) — The absolute elevation difference between reach endpoints divided by the total reach length. The simplest and most commonly used slope measure.
2. Equal Area Slope — The slope of a line through the outlet that creates equal areas above and below the longitudinal elevation profile. Adopted in Australian Rainfall and Runoff (ARR, 1987) for the Bransby Williams time-of-concentration formula. Reference: Ladson (2017), NZ Ministry of Works (1980).
Both methods compute slope internally as dimensionless values (m/m). A new Output unit option lets you choose between m/m (dimensionless) and % (percent) — the result is multiplied by 100 when percent is selected. Slope values are added as new fields on a copy of the input reach layer. DEM elevation is sampled at a user-defined interval along each reach using trapezoidal integration for the Equal Area Slope.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Routing Plan
pyqgis_plugin.description: Routing, isochrones, OD matrix, map matching, and elevation analysis powered by Valhalla and OSRM. Works globally via OSRM, with deep Valhalla support for Indonesia and any self-hosted Valhalla server.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Plugin for routing waypoints (CSV/XLSX/GeoJSON/KML) with turn-by-turn directions like Google Maps. Supports dual routing engines (Valhalla + OSRM), route optimization, isochrones, OD matrix, map matching, elevation profiles, and snap-to-road utility.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS2Blender
pyqgis_plugin.description: This plugin prepares DEMs for use in Blender.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS2Blender prepares DEM rasters for Blender heightmap workflows. It can mosaic multiple DEMs with a VRT, reproject to a target CRS, optionally clip by polygon AOI, fill NoData pixels before scaling, and export a UInt16 GeoTIFF scaled to 0-65535. No external Python dependencies are required.

pyqgis_plugin.name: qOLS
pyqgis_plugin.description: Obstacle Limitation Surfaces plugin for QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin allows calculation and visualization of various OLS (Obstacle Limitation Surfaces) for aerodrome analysis. Features include navigation between different surface types, parameter customization, and export options.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Georeferencer Autosave
pyqgis_plugin.description: Automatically saves GCP points while working in the QGIS Georeferencer, preventing loss of work from crashes or accidental closure.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Hooks into the QGIS Georeferencer and autosaves GCP points to the standard .points file whenever changes are detected. If QGIS crashes or the Georeferencer is accidentally closed, just reopen and load GCPs as normal. A timestamp can be shown in the Georeferencer status bar so you always know when the last autosave fired.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SDU Agro Tools
pyqgis_plugin.description: A collection of tools for agricultural use. Including color segmentation and crop row detection.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Precision agriculture application. This plug-in segments the raster layer based on a color distribution calculated from a shape file or a cropped image over the raster layer. Can detect crop rows on a grayscale raster layer from color distribution calculations. This plugin uses to Qpip plugin to install the following python packages. CDC, crop-row-detector and shapely. Some of the python packages may already be installed but the Qpip plugin will handle installing missing packages.

pyqgis_plugin.name: qrigeo
pyqgis_plugin.description: Interpolation toolbox for QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: A collection of QGIS processings for basic interpolation, including universal kriging and fault network capabilities.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Itinera – Least-Cost Pathways
pyqgis_plugin.description: Least-Cost Path, Corridor (LCC), FETE, Randomized Shortest Paths, circuit-theory connectivity, multi-criteria cost surfaces, sensitivity analysis and route validation (PDI + buffer overlap) for archaeological movement modelling.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Anisotropic cost-surface analysis using scipy.sparse. Provides Processing algorithms (Slope Cost Surface, Friction Cost Surface, Composite friction (multi-criteria), Accessibility / cost catchment, LCP, Stochastic LCP, Corridor, FETE, Randomized Shortest Paths, Circuit current density / pinch points, Connectivity barriers / restoration, Sensitivity Analysis, PDI Validation, Buffer Validation, Resample DEM, DEM error realisation) with ten cost functions (Tobler on/off-path, Herzog, Naismith, Llobera & Sluckin, Irmischer & Clarke, Minetti, load-aware Pandolf, and Wheeled / Pack animal critical-slope presets), plus an interactive map-click tool for point-to-point LCP. RSP adds a theta parameter spanning the least-cost-path and circuit-theory extremes; circuit theory adds current density, pinch points and barrier/restoration maps; the multi-criteria builder combines several penalty rasters into one composite friction; the stochastic DEM-error model uses true variogram (FFT spectral) random fields; accessibility produces cost catchments and isochrones. No external pip dependencies required (uses numpy/scipy bundled with QGIS). Released under a split licence: reusable core MIT; QGIS plugin GPLv3.

pyqgis_plugin.name: AgenticGIS
pyqgis_plugin.description: An in-QGIS agentic chat assistant that operates QGIS via PyQGIS. Connect with an API key, compatible endpoint, or local CLI agent.
pyqgis_plugin.about: AgenticGIS adds a chat dock to QGIS. Type a request in natural language and an LLM agent carries it out by generating and running PyQGIS code, giving it access to QGIS, Processing, project layers, and installed plugins. Requirements: QGIS 3.22 or newer (including QGIS 4) and an LLM connection using a provider API key, compatible custom endpoint, or installed local CLI agent. The plugin has no bundled Python package dependencies. Google Earth Engine features are optional and require the Google Earth Engine QGIS plugin to be installed and authenticated separately.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Arraymaker
pyqgis_plugin.description: Makes points in a circle around a central point
pyqgis_plugin.about: Defines points on a circle. Define radius of circle and number of points. Click once for the centre point and once in the direction of the first point

pyqgis_plugin.name: Velantis Wind
pyqgis_plugin.description: Wind-farm pre-assessment in QGIS: Energy/AEP, Noise and Shadow Flicker workflows.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Experimental open-source QGIS plugin for early-stage wind-farm pre-assessment. It includes Energy/AEP workflows, wind-turbine noise screening and shadow flicker analysis. This package is marked as compatible with QGIS 3.x and QGIS 4.x. A Qt5/Qt6 compatibility layer is included, but QGIS 4 support should still be validated with real installations and user feedback. Important installation note: the Energy/AEP module requires PyWake to be installed separately in the same Python environment used by QGIS. PyWake is not a QGIS plugin and will not appear in the QGIS plugin manager. On Windows, open OSGeo4W Shell and run: python -m pip install py_wake==2.6.18. Then restart QGIS. Noise and Shadow Flicker can be tested independently without PyWake. This experimental release is intended for screening, layout comparison, workflow testing and technical feedback. It is not certified regulatory or bankable assessment software. Full installation instructions, documentation and troubleshooting are available on the project website and GitHub repository.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Isoliner - грид и изолинии
pyqgis_plugin.description: 2D kriging (GSLIB KB2D) and isoline / contour-polygon generation in QGIS. Кригинг 2D (GSLIB KB2D) и построение изолиний/контурных полигонов в QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: A Processing toolset for point-data interpolation and isolines. It holds 2D kriging (points to raster, GSLIB KB2D core), the experimental variogram with model fitting and leave-one-out cross-validation. Next come optional trend removal (regression kriging), isolines and contour polygons whose boundaries coincide with the lines, reusable processing profiles and a sample-data generator. Suitable for roof elevations, thicknesses, geomechanical properties, chemistry and any numeric attribute. Bilingual (EN/RU) user manual (PDF) is bundled. The interface language and the help language can be chosen separately and by default follow QGIS. Two companion plugins work alongside it: Isoliner3D (https://github.com/Valery35/qgis-isoliner3d) shows the surfaces and bodies in a 3D scene, and Topoliner (https://github.com/Valery35/topoliner) puts the topology of polygon and line layers in order before interpolation. Developed with the support of Inform++ LLC (www.informpp.ru). . Группа команд Processing для интерполяции точечных данных и построения изолиний. В набор входят 2D Kriging (точки в растр, ядро GSLIB KB2D), экспериментальная вариограмма с подбором модели и кросс-валидация (leave-one-out). Дальше идут необязательное снятие тренда (регрессия-кригинг), изолинии и контурные полигоны с совпадающими границами, профили обработки и генератор учебных данных. Подходит для отметок пласта, мощностей, ФМС, химии и любых числовых атрибутов. Двуязычное руководство пользователя (PDF, EN/RU) в комплекте. Язык интерфейса и язык справки выбираются отдельно и по умолчанию идут за QGIS. Рядом работают два плагина того же набора: Isoliner3D (https://github.com/Valery35/qgis-isoliner3d) показывает поверхности и тела в 3D-сцене, а Topoliner (https://github.com/Valery35/topoliner) приводит в порядок топологию полигональных и линейных слоёв перед интерполяцией. Разработано при поддержке ООО «Информ++» (www.informpp.ru).

pyqgis_plugin.name: HeatScape
pyqgis_plugin.description: HeatScape is a QGIS plugin for Land Surface Temperature, UHI, and UHII analysis from Landsat 8/9 thermal imagery.
pyqgis_plugin.about: HeatScape calculates Land Surface Temperature (LST), Urban Heat Island (UHI) maps, and Urban Heat Island Intensity (UHII) statistics from Landsat 8/9 Band 10 rasters.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Arif K Wijayanto, Divisi Analisis Lingkungan dan Geospasial Modeling, IPB University

pyqgis_plugin.name: QCity
pyqgis_plugin.description: Urban development modeling in QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about: QCity is a QGIS plugin that allows for the modeling of constructed, proposed and potential buildings based on approved plans or the urban planning framework. QCity calculates dwelling yield, commercial floorspace yield and parking yield of building levels based the percentage of each floor assigned to different land uses and assumptions provided by the user and then aggregates the dwelling yield, commercial floorspace yield and parking yield for each development site. QCity also aggregates the dwelling yield, commercial floorspace yield and parking yield over a project area incorporating multiple development sites. Modeled buildings can also be visualized in a QGIS 3D map in combination with other spatial data. <b>Please note that currently the plugin has been designed for use in Australia only, we plan on expanding this to allow use in other regions before the initial stable release.</b>

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeolAttitude
pyqgis_plugin.description: Plugin for for interactive estimation the attitude of geologic planar features from DTMs. Implements user-selectable fitting methods and uncertainty analysis. It is developed by a geologist, for geologists with the right attitude!
pyqgis_plugin.about: Interactive plug-in for photogeologic interpretations of geologic planar features. Computes geologic structures dip, dip direction and strike from interactively selected points sampled from a DTM raster. Click points on imagery or map canvas, sample elevation from a selected DTM, fit a best-fit plane and compute structural attitude parameters. Designed for terrestrial and planetary projected DTMs. Implements user-selectable fitting methods. Implements user-selectable fitting methods.

pyqgis_plugin.name: FraXtex
pyqgis_plugin.description: Automatic geological fracture mapping from an RGB orthophoto, with or without a DEM
pyqgis_plugin.about: FraXtex is a QGIS 3/4 plugin for automatic fracture mapping in two stages: (1) generate a fracture probability map from an RGB orthophoto, with or without a DEM, using ONNX deep learning models (3-channel RGB and 4-channel RGB+DEM models are both supported; the right one is read from the model's declared input shape, falling back to whether a DEM was supplied when the model exports that dimension symbolically), and (2) vectorize the probability map into LineString geometry. Dependencies (numpy, rasterio, scikit-image, onnxruntime, geopandas, shapely, pygeoops) are auto-installed on first run via pip. If auto-install fails, a platform-specific manual command is shown in the Processing log. See the README for manual install instructions for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

pyqgis_plugin.name: niva
pyqgis_plugin.description: QGIS from the command line: write concise text-pipeline geoprocessing flows (no PyQGIS coding) and run them in a dock.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS from the command line. A concise, readable text-pipeline grammar for QGIS geoprocessing (load … | buffer 100m dissolve | save …) that stands on PyQGIS, but for people who don't write PyQGIS. Reach ~878 QGIS Processing algorithms through ~45 friendly verbs (or `run` any algorithm by id), across vector, raster, point clouds and databases. This plugin adds a dock where you write or open a .niva flow file and run it in the current QGIS session; results land on the map. The same grammar also runs as a standalone command-line tool and REPL (pip install qgis-niva). niva is bundled with the plugin (zero-dependency, pure Python), so there is no separate install step on Windows, macOS, or Linux. It runs in-process on QGIS's own Python and Processing algorithms and can run without QGIS itself even running (batch jobs).

pyqgis_plugin.name: 360ForYou Uploader
pyqgis_plugin.description: Upload raster, vector and point cloud layers from QGIS to a 360-for-you.com project
pyqgis_plugin.about: Uploads data from the current QGIS project to 360-for-you.com or a self-hosted 360ForYou server and creates a viewer project you can share by link. Raster layers are uploaded as GeoTIFF (rendered RGBA export, or the source file when it is already an RGB GeoTIFF), vector layers are exported to KML, point cloud layers upload their LAS/LAZ source files, and arbitrary files can be added from disk. Uploads are chunked and resumable and run in the QGIS task manager. Requires an account and an API key (Profile - API keys, scopes projects:read and projects:write). The server URL is configurable for self-hosted installations. Uses only the QGIS/Python standard library - no external dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: DigDok
pyqgis_plugin.description: Basemaps and data layers for the Norwegian cultural-heritage sector
pyqgis_plugin.about:
DigDok Maps adds one-click menu shortcuts for background maps and Norwegian open-data / cultural-heritage layers, aimed at archaeology and heritage documentation.
Norwegian sources: Riksantikvaren (kulturminner), Kartverket (topographic cache, Matrikkelen, historical maps, administrative units, elevation), NGU (geology), NIBIO (land resources), Geodata, UNIMUS (Gjenstandsbasen) and ADED (excavation data).
Global basemaps: Google, Bing, Esri, Carto, OpenStreetMap, OpenTopoMap, F4map and Stadia Maps (incl. the Stamen styles, shaded relief, terrarium and vector tilesets). Stadia layers need a free API key, set from the DigDok menu and stored in the QGIS authentication database. All layers carry attribution.
Derived from the HCMGIS plugin by Thang Quach (opengeoshub/HCMGIS, GPL-3.0): https://github.com/opengeoshub/HCMGIS

pyqgis_plugin.name: Stratified Packager
pyqgis_plugin.description: Exports vector layers to multiple geopackages split by attributes or spatial intersection
pyqgis_plugin.about: Partitions the open project’s layers against a stratification layer — by attribute (following project relations) or spatially — and publishes one zipped GeoPackage per stratum, optionally with an embedded per-stratum QGIS project, layer styles, metadata and referenced style assets. Runs from the Processing Toolbox and from qgis_process.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Computo Metrico GIS
pyqgis_plugin.description: Computo metrico e contabilita lavori in QGIS con prezziari regionali o CSV/XLSX/DCF, SAL, report PDF/XLSX e progetto dimostrativo. / Bill of quantities and works accounting in QGIS with Italian regional price lists or CSV/XLSX/DCF files, progress payments (SAL), PDF/XLSX reports and a demo project.
pyqgis_plugin.about: IT: Plugin sperimentale per computo metrico estimativo e contabilita lavori con database SQLite locale, import validato dei prezziari, misurazioni automatiche da geometrie, SAL, giornale lavori e reportistica professionale. I risultati vanno sempre verificati da un tecnico abilitato prima dell'uso contrattuale. / EN: Experimental plugin for bill of quantities and works accounting with a local SQLite database, validated price list import, automatic measurements from geometries, progress payments (SAL), works journal and professional reporting. Results must always be verified by a qualified professional before contractual use.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Isobenefit Urbanism
pyqgis_plugin.description: Sketch walkable urban growth scenarios on real-world data, after D'Acci's Isobenefit Urbanism: every new home within a walk of a mixed-use centre and of green space.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The Isobenefit Urbanism QGIS plugin explores walkable urban development against real-world datasets. It grows settlements by simple rules: every new home must sit within a walking distance of a mixed-use centre (shops, services) and of green space. The model follows Luca D'Acci's Isobenefit Urbanism (D'Acci 2019, Journal of Environmental Management; D'Acci & Voto 2023, SoftwareX) and reimplements the cellular automaton originally coded by Michele Voto, with documented departures and extensions (fixed existing fabric, OSM inputs, transit-oriented growth, centre post-processing). See the homepage for the full guide and worked scenarios. The plugin bundles an OpenStreetMap extraction tool, ships six worked scenarios in the repository's "scenarios" folder, and writes reproducible runs (each run saves a parameters sidecar that the dialog can reload). This plugin is marked experimental: enable "Show also Experimental Plugins" in the plugin manager settings to see it. On first use, the plugin offers to install its simulation engine (the "isobenefit" package from PyPI) into the QGIS Python environment; this needs an internet connection and a QGIS restart. No manual package installation is required. Licensed under the GNU AGPL-3.0-or-later (see the LICENSE file).

pyqgis_plugin.name: oceanum-datamesh
pyqgis_plugin.description: Search, query, load and display Oceanum Datamesh ocean & environmental data directly in QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: A QGIS plugin for the Oceanum Datamesh platform. Search the Datamesh catalog, inspect dataset metadata, then query and load data into QGIS as native layers: gridded datasets become raster layers, feature datasets become vector layers, and station/table data become point or attribute-table layers. Requires a Datamesh access token (set the DATAMESH_TOKEN environment variable or enter it in the plugin). Depends on the `oceanum` Python package, which the plugin can install for you on first run.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GEAQUA Capture Zones
pyqgis_plugin.description: Analytical delineation of groundwater time-of-travel capture zones for a single pumping well.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GEAQUA Capture Zones is a Polish-English QGIS tool for analytical delineation of time-of-travel capture zones for one pumping well in a homogeneous aquifer with uniform regional groundwater flow. The current method follows Ceric and Haitjema (2005) and supports centric circular, eccentric circular and uniform-flow capture-zone approximations, including the zero ambient-flow limit. The plugin is intended for screening, documentation and hydrogeological analysis. Calculated zones require professional review and are not automatically legally designated protection areas. No external Python dependencies are required.
pyqgis_plugin.tags: time of travel,well protection,pumping well,groundwater,capture zone,hydrogeology,source water,uniform flow

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS-FME Flow Connector
pyqgis_plugin.description: Run FME Flow workspaces from QGIS—export a layer, submit it via Job Submitter, and optionally load transformed results back into your map.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS-FME Flow Connector links QGIS 4 and FME Flow through the REST API. Just select a vector layer and a workspace, connect with your server URL and API token, then process your data in FME Flow as a regular FME Flow job. This plugin processes and returns data to QGIS and adds the resulting data as a layer in the QGIS project. The plugin uploads input data to shared resources, monitors job progress, supports job cancellation, and keeps connection settings and saves preferences between sessions.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SQL Database Mine
pyqgis_plugin.description: QGIS Plugin to mine related data from a SQL database server.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Mine data from selected features within a QGIS vector layer. Related data derived from a layer's Relationships and Joins can then be searched by selecting the required relationship. Once related data is searched, you can keep mining deeper with any further relationships. Where a vector layer is stored within a SQL database, the search is executed on the SQL database server, utilising the database indexes for rapid responses. If the related data has GIS features, these can be selected and zoomed into on the QGIS map. Rows of selected data can be copied into the clipboard for use in other applications. A query form is also included to enable SQL database searches and view the resulting features on the QGIS map. The inbuilt QGIS features to view table data loads and scans the layers full data, which is unusable for large datasets. SQL Database Mine performs the query on the database server and only deals with the resulting dataset. Requires Python module "sqlalchemy". This should be installed from your operating system distribution.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Kakao QGIS Bridge
pyqgis_plugin.description: Dock-based Kakao Map and Roadview viewer with bidirectional QGIS synchronization and Local search.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Shows Kakao Maps JavaScript API content inside a QGIS dock widget and synchronizes QGIS, Kakao Map, and Roadview in both directions. Includes Local place/address search, Roadview position/direction display, Kakao Mobility route search, route guidance, and route history import/export. Requires user-provided Kakao JavaScript and REST API keys. Kakao tile URLs are not extracted or used as XYZ/TMS layers.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Military Cartography Tools
pyqgis_plugin.description: Military cartography, MIL-STD-2525D/E and APP-6D/E tactical graphics, MGRS, and terrain analysis tools for QGIS. Runs fully offline - no external services, no data ever leaves your machine.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Military Cartography Tools (MCT) is a QGIS plugin providing tools for military mapping, including MIL-STD-2525D/E and APP-6D/E tactical graphics (control measures and entity symbols, drawn as real QGIS symbology rather than stamped images, so they scale and print correctly at any map scale, with a per-layer edition switch to choose which standard a symbology layer is built against), MGRS coordinate handling, military grid generation, layout automation, coordinate conversion, cartographic utilities, terrain analysis (illuminated contours, hypsometric tint, line of sight, combined hillshade, and viewshed/dead-ground analysis), and navigation/production tools (bearing/range, GPX/KML waypoint import/export, and batch print-sheet generation tiling a large area). Every tool runs entirely offline against local data - GDAL/QGIS Processing, a bundled World Magnetic Model, and your own DEM - with no external services, API calls, or telemetry of any kind, making it suitable for use with sensitive or classified data.

pyqgis_plugin.name: WAI QGIS MCP
pyqgis_plugin.description: Let trusted AI assistants inspect, map, and automate QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about: WAI QGIS MCP lets trusted AI assistants inspect projects, manage layers, run Processing algorithms, render maps, and execute PyQGIS code. It can run arbitrary PyQGIS code, so only connect assistants you trust. Setup: open Plugins > WAI QGIS MCP > WAI QGIS MCP, click Start Server, then use the "Assistant setup help" button in that panel for the exact command for your assistant. In short: Claude Desktop installs a .mcpb extension from the latest GitHub release and needs no separate Node.js. Claude Code, the Codex CLI and the ChatGPT desktop app need Node.js 18+ and run the server with npx. In the ChatGPT desktop app, add the server under Settings > Plugins > MCPs and use Work mode, because Chat mode cannot see local MCP servers. Keep QGIS running on the same computer as the assistant. See the homepage for complete setup and troubleshooting.

pyqgis_plugin.name: LiDAR AutoVector Studio
pyqgis_plugin.description: Interactive LiDAR-to-vector automation with independent extraction of water, vegetation, low vegetation, settlements, buildings, cropland, bare land, roads and elevated linear features.
pyqgis_plugin.about: LiDAR AutoVector Studio converts LAS, LAZ, COPC and EPT point clouds into terrain derivatives and independently selectable vector feature candidates. It generates DTM, DSM, CHM, density, roughness and slope layers, then extracts water bodies, tall vegetation, low vegetation, settlement areas, buildings, cropland, bare land, roads/open surfaces and elevated linear features. Outputs are separate GeoPackage layers and require validation against imagery or field observations. External dependency: PDAL available in the QGIS or OSGeo4W environment.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Mr. Akmaul Hoque; Dr. Manish Kumar Naskar; Dr. Debashis Chakraborty

pyqgis_plugin.name: HYDRA2DGPU
pyqgis_plugin.description: GPU-accelerated 2D shallow water equation solver for QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about:
HYDRA2DGPU performs 2D hydrodynamic flood and surface-water modelling using a CUDA finite-volume solver. It couples unstructured meshes, 1D drainage networks, hydraulic structures, and rainfall / infiltration, all inside the QGIS map canvas.
This plugin requires an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support (compute capability >= 7.5). On first launch the plugin installs the hydra-swe2d solver backend into an isolated per-user Python environment; Windows and Linux x86_64 are supported, macOS is not.
Manual / advanced install: see https://github.com/aspragueumkc/hydra2dgpu#readme.

pyqgis_plugin.name: KrigMultiProfile
pyqgis_plugin.description: Batch ordinary kriging of geochemical elements with automatic BG/TH statistics and lithogeochemical map+profile generation.
pyqgis_plugin.about: KrigMultiProfile takes a geochemical point layer and, in one Processing algorithm, computes BG/TH statistics (log10, Tukey and log-gap outlier detection), runs ordinary kriging per element, and generates map+profile PNG sheets combined with a lithology layer along user-defined profile lines. Designed for exploration geochemistry with small sample sets. Each step (statistics, kriging, map+profile) is also available as its own algorithm for finer control.

pyqgis_plugin.name: OpenStaR-Elec Déploiement
pyqgis_plugin.description: Create a business environment within an "OpenStaR-Elec Récolement" QGIS profile for mapping electrical networks in StaR-Elec, the new French geostandard dedicated to electricity networks.
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin adds a toolbar button that creates (if necessary) the "OpenStaR-Elec Récolement" QGIS profile and downloads/installs the latest version of the openstar_elec_rec extension within it.

pyqgis_plugin.name: ArcGIS-like Workspace
pyqgis_plugin.description: Applies an ArcGIS Pro-inspired workspace preset and behavior to QGIS using native QGIS actions, toolbars, dock widgets, settings, and Qt styling.
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin rearranges QGIS into an ArcGIS Pro-inspired workspace and layers on genuine behavioral parity (contextual ribbon, Labeling toggle, Notifications, unified search, opt-in shortcuts) while keeping QGIS behavior native and reversible. It does not include Esri assets, branding, or proprietary UI code.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QuickShapeStatistics
pyqgis_plugin.description: Draw quick shapes to be used for simple zonal statistics.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Click a button to draw a circle or a polygon shape, which will be used to calculate basic zonal statistics on the active layer. For polygons the area will be calculated, for lines the length will be used and for points the number of points will be summarized.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Terrain Product Studio
pyqgis_plugin.description: Publication-grade terrain maps from one DEM: 20 color palettes, USGS-style cartography, hydrology, geomorphometry, multi-hazard analysis, GeoPackage bundles, QGIS project export, 3D web viewers, restyle-without-regeneration and STL/OBJ print models.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Terrain Product Studio turns one elevation raster into a full set of publication-ready layers: elevation color relief, hillshades, slope, aspect, TRI/TPI, roughness, curvatures, spot elevations, smoothed contours and rivers, geomorphons, SPI/STI, landslide and multi-hazard indexes, hydrology, an all-in-one GeoPackage bundle, a ready-to-save .qgz project and an interactive 3D web viewer. The Assistant tab suggests smart defaults (contour interval, stream threshold, river width/depth, working CRS) from your DEM; cartography can be restyled onto existing canvas, QML and print layouts without re-running the pipeline. 20 color ramps in Light/Dark/Scientific, one-click industry presets, STL/OBJ 3D-print export and a run-history journal.

pyqgis_plugin.name: aXqua
pyqgis_plugin.description: Set up, run and monitor TELEMAC and OpenFOAM river models from QGIS, with jobs that keep running after QGIS is closed.
pyqgis_plugin.about: aXqua turns geodata into a calibration-ready hydro- and morphodynamic model (TELEMAC-2D/3D with GAIA, or an OpenFOAM interFoam free-surface case) and drives it through a persistent job runner. Simulations are launched as detached system jobs, so they survive closing QGIS, and are rediscovered with their live state when you reopen it. Results load back as styled mesh, raster and vector layers. The plugin does not run solvers itself: it talks to the separately installed `axqua` command-line tool, so QGIS's Python never has to become the solver's Python. Requires the aXqua command-line tool, installed separately with 'pip install git+https://github.com/sschwindt/aXqua.git' (it is not on PyPI yet), plus a working TELEMAC and/or OpenFOAM installation.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoDeploy
pyqgis_plugin.description: Browse a GeoDeploy instance, add its layers, and publish layers back to it.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GeoDeploy is a self-hosted spatial data platform and geoportal builder. This plugin connects QGIS to an instance: browse what it publishes (no account needed for public data), add a layer using the fastest source it offers, and upload a QGIS layer back — including multi-gigabyte files, which go straight to object storage. Pure Python, no external dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: qPansopy
pyqgis_plugin.description: QPANSOPY Plugin for QGIS - Procedure Analysis and Obstacle Protection Surfaces (PANSOPS)
pyqgis_plugin.about: QPANSOPY Plugin for QGIS to create aviation surfaces including VSS, OCS, ILS, OAS, Wind Spiral and PBN-LNAV protection surfaces according to ICAO PANS-OPS Doc 8168 standards.

pyqgis_plugin.name: qAeroChart
pyqgis_plugin.description: ICAO Aeronautical Chart Plugin - Create approach profiles and aeronautical charts
pyqgis_plugin.about: Plugin for creating aeronautical charts following ICAO Annex 4 and Doc 8697 standards and industry best practices

pyqgis_plugin.name: Logis
pyqgis_plugin.description: QGIS plugin for logistics in Brazil, supporting urban logistics, regional logistics, and waste collection routing.
pyqgis_plugin.about: logis is a QGIS plugin designed to support logistics projects in Brazil. It consists of three modules: Urban Logistics (OSM-based), Regional Logistics (DNIT/SNV-based), and Specialized Logistics (waste collection routing). The plugin provides tools for calculating logistics indicators, vehicle routing (VRP/TSP), and facility location (p-median, MCLP, LSCP) using PyQGIS and Python's standard library.

pyqgis_plugin.name: AirEmergency
pyqgis_plugin.description: Rapid atmospheric dispersion model for emergency response based on Gaussian plume equations.
pyqgis_plugin.about: AirEmergency is a QGIS plugin implementing a Gaussian plume approach for rapid atmospheric dispersion assessments in emergency situations. The plugin is intended for screening-level and expedited analyses, providing a fast estimation of airborne concentrations and dry deposition from accidental releases, fires, or other emergency scenarios. AirEmergency is NOT intended for detailed regulatory assessments, environmental impact studies, permitting applications, or planning activities requiring high-accuracy modeling. For such purposes, more advanced and thoroughly validated models (e.g. AERMOD, CALPUFF or equivalent regulatory models) should be used. Main features include ground-level concentration estimation, dry deposition estimation, Buoyant plume rise from fire heat release, terrain correction through DEM integration, direct GIS visualization of results within QGIS. Results should be considered indicative and suitable for emergency response, situational awareness, preliminary decision support, and rapid screening analyses. (Turner, D.B. (1994). Workbook of Atmospheric Dispersion Estimates: An Introduction to Dispersion Modeling (2nd Edition). CRC Press;Seinfeld, J.H., Pandis, S.N. (2016). Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics: From Air Pollution to Climate Change (3rd Edition). Wiley. U.S. EPA (2023). Guideline on Air Quality Models, Appendix W to 40 CFR Part 51.)

pyqgis_plugin.name: RapidIBF-Next
pyqgis_plugin.description: This plugin turns raw hazard and exposure data into simple, decision-ready impact estimates. Instead of stopping at "where the hazard will occur", it helps answer "who and what is likely to be affected, and by how much", so that governments and sector agencies can act early and target resources where they matter most. Includes tools for data classification, zonal statistics, and report generation.
pyqgis_plugin.about: RapidIBF-Next is an impact-based forecasting (IBF) toolkit for national hydro-meteorological services, disaster management offices and sector agencies. It combines a hazard layer (for example a seasonal climate outlook, a rainfall or temperature anomaly, a flood or landslide susceptibility raster, or a tropical cyclone wind swath) with exposure data (population rasters, point facilities such as schools and health centres, or line networks such as roads) and aggregates the result to administrative boundaries. Workflows cover raster hazard with raster exposure, raster hazard with point exposure, and raster hazard with line exposure. Outputs include classified impact layers styled in QGIS, GeoPackage and CSV exports, and a comprehensive HTML and PDF report with maps, charts and summary text. The report is available in English, Russian, Hindi, Tamil, Sinhala and Dhivehi, with terminology drawn from official government and disaster-risk-reduction sources. The plugin uses only libraries bundled with QGIS (GDAL, NumPy and Jinja2). No additional Python packages need to be installed. Developed by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP).

pyqgis_plugin.name: ReliefEnergy
pyqgis_plugin.description: Relief energy processing tool
pyqgis_plugin.about: A processing plugin using built in processing tools and a user provided DEM+ area of interest, to calculate the relief energy of the AoI, for use in geomorphological or other studies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QCALVIEW
pyqgis_plugin.description: Photographic viewpoint calibration, visual simulation and projected GIS overlays directly in QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: QCALVIEW ALPHA-40.20.5 is an experimental open-source QGIS plugin for photographic viewpoint calibration, visual simulation, projected vector overlays, schematic representations and rapid landscape visualisation workflows. Compatible with QGIS 3.44/Qt5 and QGIS 4.x/Qt6. Licensed under GNU GPL v3 or later. Documentation: qcalview.com.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Spot Level & Contour Extractor Tool
pyqgis_plugin.description: Extract regularly-gridded spot levels and elevation contour lines from a DSM/DTM raster, in any coordinate system.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Two Processing algorithms for drone/photogrammetry survey workflows: (1) Spot Levels - samples elevation at a regular grid interval (1m, 2m, 3m, or any custom spacing) and exports points as CSV, Shapefile, and/or KML; (2) Contours - generates elevation contour lines at a chosen interval and exports them as Shapefile, DXF, DWG, and/or KML. Both accept a raster in any coordinate system: a raster in a geographic CRS (plain latitude/longitude degrees) is automatically reprojected in memory to the correct UTM zone first, so interval/spacing values are always true metres on the ground. Requires a handful of third-party Python packages (rasterio, geopandas, scipy, contourpy, ezdxf, pyogrio) to be installed into QGIS's own Python environment - see the plugin's README for the one-time setup command.

pyqgis_plugin.name: geobr
pyqgis_plugin.description: Download official spatial data sets of Brazil as QGIS layers
pyqgis_plugin.about: Easy access to official spatial data sets of Brazil. The plugin offers a wide range of official spatial data sets available at various geographic scales and for various years with harmonized attributes, projection and fixed topology. This includes states, municipalities, census tracts, biomes, indigenous lands, health facilities, schools, favelas and more. All original data sets come from IBGE and other official Brazilian sources and are returned in EPSG:4674 (SIRGAS 2000). This QGIS plugin is built on top of the geobr Python library, which integrates seamlessly with DuckDB and geopandas, and can be used from the Processing Toolbox, chained in Model Builder, run in batch, or called from qgis_process. The geobr library is bundled with the plugin, so there is nothing to pip-install. DuckDB, the engine geobr runs on, is installed for you by the qpip plugin, which QGIS offers to install alongside this one; if you skip qpip, install it into the Python QGIS uses: python -m pip install --user "duckdb>=1.5.3". Everything else geobr needs ships with the official QGIS builds for Windows and macOS; a Linux distribution build of QGIS may lack geopandas or pyarrow, and the plugin says so at startup.

pyqgis_plugin.name: EMBED-CD
pyqgis_plugin.description: Change maps from satellite embeddings. Draw an area, pick two years, then label a few objects and a live classifier labels the rest on the fly.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Generates year-over-year land change maps from AlphaEarth satellite embeddings (Google Satellite Embedding V1), which cover the globe for every year 2017-2025 at 10 m. Works tile by tile and fills the canvas as each tile completes, so memory stays flat and large areas are possible. Missing data is shown as its own class, never as "no change". Label a few change objects and a live one-vs-rest classifier labels the rest on the fly. CPU-only, nothing to train, no account or API key - data is read directly from public cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs, and the one-time tile index is a small pre-built file needing only numpy. Tested on Windows (QGIS 3.44 and 4.0). macOS is untested; Linux support is planned for a later release. The AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding dataset is produced by Google and Google DeepMind (CC BY 4.0).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Forest Planner
pyqgis_plugin.description: From forest census to management plan: drainage network, riparian buffers, log landings, skid trails, haul roads and impact areas for Amazonian forest management.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Forest Planner automates the analysis chain behind an Amazonian forest management plan. From a digital elevation model and the forest census layer, it derives the drainage network and riparian buffers by Strahler order, estimates wetlands and flood-prone ground through HAND, locates log landings and log yards under volume, skidding distance and slope constraints, builds a traversability cost surface and lays out the haul road network, then consolidates impact areas, harvest intensity and transport trips. . DEL CENSO FORESTAL AL PLAN DE MANEJO. Automatiza la cadena de analisis que sostiene un plan de manejo forestal amazonico: red hidrica y fajas marginales por orden de Strahler, aguajales y zonas inundables mediante HAND, patios y centros de acopio con restricciones de volumen y arrastre, superficie de costo y red de vias, areas de impacto, intensidad de aprovechamiento y viajes de transporte. . CALIBRACION VERIFICABLE: los parametros por defecto no son supuestos. El umbral de cauce reproduce el 86.8% de una quebrada levantada en campo; el arrastre medio da 162 m frente a los 160 m de Braz (1997); el area de patios da 18.7 m2/ha frente a los 24 de Johns et al. (1996); y la densidad vial da 15.0 m/ha frente a los 13.2 y 15.3 medidos en dos parcelas de corta reales de Madre de Dios, una de las cuales NO se uso para calibrar. . HONESTIDAD DE LOS RESULTADOS: los trazos son propuestas sujetas a replanteo en campo y el informe lo declara. Las distancias de arrastre se declaran como euclidianas. El area basal removida y la abundancia por especie se reportan como NO CONCLUYENTES cuando el insumo es un censo comercial, porque ese dato no puede sustentarlas. Los diametros minimos de corta se presentan como el minimo legal y no como el sostenible. Cada insumo se acredita en el informe con su SHA-256, y las capas en memoria se declaran como no verificables en lugar de inventarles un identificador. . ALCANCE REGIONAL: incluye limites normativos de Peru, Brasil, Bolivia y Ecuador, cada uno con la norma que lo sustenta. Los diametros minimos de corta del Peru provienen de la RJ 458-2002-INRENA. . SIN DEPENDENCIAS OBLIGATORIAS: solo requiere numpy y scipy, incluidos en QGIS, y el proveedor GRASS para la hidrologia. El complemento verifica el entorno y senala lo que falte. . MANUAL COMPLETO: https://github.com/YuriCaller/yf_forest_planner/blob/main/docs . Desarrollado en Puerto Maldonado, Madre de Dios, sobre censos reales de concesiones forestales de la Amazonia peruana.
